    19:     complyctl_bin: "{{ lookup('env', 'COMPLYCTL_BIN') | default('/tmp/complyctl', true) }}"
    20:     provider_bin: "{{ lookup('env', 'PROVIDER_BIN') | default(ansible_env.HOME + '/.complytime/providers/complyctl-provider-openscap', true) }}"

    62:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    63:     # OCI registry — distribution/distribution binary (no podman required).

    97:               rootdirectory: /var/lib/gemara-registry

   100:           http:

    51:           -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT

   168:   - name: 'freshclam (seed the signature database so clamd can start)'

   173:       - 'clamav__clamd_service_enabled | bool'

   175:   - name: 'systemctl {{ clamav__clamd_service_enabled | bool | ternary("enable", "disable") }} {{ __clamav__clamd_service }}'

   191: 
   192:   - name: 'systemctl {{ clamav__clamonacc_service_state | regex_replace("p?ed$", "") }} clamav-clamonacc.service'

   194:       name: 'clamav-clamonacc.service'
   195:       state: '{{ clamav__clamonacc_service_state }}'
   196:     register: '__clamav__clamonacc_service_state_result'
   197: 
   198:   - name: 'systemctl {{ clamav__clamdscan_timer_enabled | bool | ternary("enable", "disable") }} --now clamav-clamdscan.timer'

   202:       state: '{{ clamav__clamdscan_timer_enabled | bool | ternary("started", "stopped") }}'
   203:       daemon_reload: '{{ clamav__systemd_clamdscan_timer_result is changed }}'
   204: 
   205:   - name: 'systemctl {{ clamav__freshclam_service_enabled | bool | ternary("enable", "disable") }} --now clamav-freshclam.service'

   207:       name: 'clamav-freshclam.service'

   216: - block:
   217: 
   218:   # Self-test: confirm the engine plus signature database actually detect malware,
   219:   # using the EICAR test string. We feed it to the standalone `clamscan` over stdin

   221:   # VirusEvent (a "malware found" mail on every run) and, with on-access scanning

   226:     ansible.builtin.command: 'clamscan --no-summary -'
   227:     args:

   229:     register: '__clamav__eicar_result'
   230:     changed_when: false
   231:     failed_when: '"FOUND" not in __clamav__eicar_result["stdout"]'

   233:   tags:
   234:     - 'clamav'
   235:     - 'clamav:test'

review_question: Would an Ansible expert judge this playbook or task file as needing abstraction because it contains too many direct leaf tasks?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: - name: Create list of domains to request certificates for
     3:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
     4:     haproxy_ssl_hosts: >
     5:       {{
     6:         (
     7:           [base_domain]
     8:           + (haproxy_applications               | map(attribute='vhost_name') | list)
     9:           + (haproxy_ldap_servers | default([]) | map(attribute='vhost_name') | list)
    10:           + (haproxy_redirects                  | map(attribute='hostname')   | list)
    11:         )
    12:         | unique | sort
    13:       }}
    14: 
    15: - name: "print all active TLS hosts"
    16:   debug:
    17:     var: "haproxy_ssl_hosts"
    18: 
    19: ##############################################################################
    20: ## cleaning up
    21: ##############################################################################
    22: - name: "Get list of all current certificates on disk"
    23:   ansible.builtin.find:
    24:     paths: "/etc/haproxy/certs"
    25:     patterns: "*.pem"
    26:   register: "haproxy_current_certs_disk"
    27: 
    28: - name: "Backup obsolete certificates"
    29:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    30:     src: "/etc/haproxy/certs/{{ item }}.pem"
    31:     dest: "/etc/haproxy/certs-backup/{{ item }}.pem.{{ now().strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S') }}"
    32:     remote_src: true
    33:     mode: "0600"
    34:     owner: "root"
    35:     group: "root"
    36:   when: "item not in haproxy_ssl_hosts"
    37:   loop: "{{ haproxy_current_certs_disk.files | map(attribute='path') | map('basename') | map('regex_replace', '\\.pem$', '') }}"
    38: 
    39: - name: "Remove obsolete certificates from disk"
    40:   ansible.builtin.file:
    41:     path: "/etc/haproxy/certs/{{ item }}.pem"
    42:     state: "absent"
    43:   when: "item not in haproxy_ssl_hosts"
    44:   loop: "{{ haproxy_current_certs_disk.files | map(attribute='path') | map('basename') | map('regex_replace', '\\.pem$', '') }}"
    45: 
    46: - name: "Get list of all current certificates known to acme"
    47:   ansible.builtin.command:
    48:     cmd: >
    49:       /home/acme/.acme.sh/acme.sh --list
    50:   changed_when: false
    51:   failed_when: 'haproxy_acme_certs_raw.rc != 0'
    52:   check_mode: false  # this is safe run run, even in check mode
    53:   become_user: "acme"
    54:   become: true
    55:   register: "haproxy_acme_certs_raw"
    56: 
    57: # parse the output from acme.sh (skip header line, extract first column)
    58: - name: "Extract list of certificate names known to acme"
    59:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    60:     haproxy_current_acme_certs: >-
    61:       {{ haproxy_acme_certs_raw.stdout_lines[1:]
    62:          | reject('equalto', '')
    63:          | map('regex_replace', '^(\S+)\s.*$', '\1')
    64:          | list }}
    65: 
    66: - name: "Remove obsolete certs from acme.sh"
    67:   ansible.builtin.command:
    68:     cmd: >
    69:       /home/acme/.acme.sh/acme.sh --remove --domain '{{ item }}'
    70:   changed_when: "haproxy_acme_remove_certs.rc == 0"
    71:   failed_when: 'haproxy_acme_remove_certs.rc != 0'
    72:   when: "item not in haproxy_ssl_hosts"
    73:   loop: "{{ haproxy_current_acme_certs }}"
    74:   become_user: "acme"
    75:   become: true
    76:   register: "haproxy_acme_remove_certs"
    77: 
    78: 
    79: ##############################################################################
    80: ## get new certs
    81: ##############################################################################
    82: - name: Check existence of acme CNAME records
    83:   ansible.builtin.command:
    84:     cmd: "dig +short -t CNAME '_acme-challenge.{{ item }}'"
    85:   register: haproxy_acme_cname
    86:   failed_when: "haproxy_acme_cname.stdout == ''"
    87:   changed_when: false
    88:   loop: "{{ haproxy_ssl_hosts }}"
    89:   become: false
    90:   delegate_to: "localhost"
    91:   check_mode: false  # this is safe run run, even in check mode
    92:   run_once: true
    93: 
    94: - name: Update certificates on one host at a time
    95:   throttle: 1
    96:   block:
    97:     - name: Issue the certificates using acme
    98:       ansible.builtin.command:
    99:         cmd: |
   100:           /home/acme/.acme.sh/acme.sh
   101:             --issue
   102:             --ecc
   103:             --keylength ec-256
   104:             --days "{{ haproxy_acme_renewal_days }}"
   105:             --dns dns_acmedns
   106:             --stateless
   107:             --dnssleep 3
   108:             --server "{{ haproxy_acme_server }}"
   109:             --domain "{{ item }}"
   110:             {{ acme_account.changed | ternary('--force', '') }}
   111:       environment:
   112:         ACMEDNS_BASE_URL: "{{ haproxy_acmedns.baseurl }}"
   113:         ACMEDNS_USERNAME: "{{ haproxy_acmedns.username }}"
   114:         ACMEDNS_PASSWORD: "{{ haproxy_acmedns.password }}"
   115:         ACMEDNS_SUBDOMAIN: "{{ haproxy_acmedns.subdomain }}"
   116:       loop: "{{ haproxy_ssl_hosts }}"
   117:       throttle: 1
   118:       register: "acme_issue"
   119:       changed_when: "acme_issue.rc == 0"
   120:       failed_when: 'acme_issue.rc != 0 and acme_issue.rc != 2'
   121:       become_user: "acme"
   122:       become: true
   123: 
   124:     # Now deploy the certificates to haproxy
   125:     # We do this in two steps:
   126:     # 1. Cold-deploy the certificates to haproxy's certs directory
   127:     # 2. Make sure haproxy is started, and hot-deploy the certificates to haproxy though the socket API
   128: 
   129:     - name: Cold-deploy the certificates to haproxy  # noqa: no-handler
   130:       ansible.builtin.command:
   131:         cmd: |
   132:           /home/acme/.acme.sh/acme.sh
   133:             --deploy
   134:             --deploy-hook haproxy
   135:             --domain "{{ item }}"
   136:       environment:
   137:         DEPLOY_HAPROXY_PEM_PATH: "/etc/haproxy/certs"
   138:       loop: "{{ haproxy_ssl_hosts }}"
   139:       register: "result"
   140:       changed_when: "result.rc == 0"
   141:       when: "acme_issue.changed"
   142:       become_user: "acme"
   143:       become: true
   144: 
   145:     - name: Start and enable haproxy
   146:       ansible.builtin.service:
   147:         name: "haproxy"
   148:         state: "started"
   149:         enabled: true
   150: 
   151:     - name: Wait for port 443 to become open  # noqa: no-handler
   152:       ansible.builtin.wait_for:
   153:         port: 443
   154:         delay: 5
   155:         host: "{{ haproxy_sni_ip.ipv4 }}"
   156:       when: "acme_issue.changed"
   157: 
   158:     - name: Hot-deploy the certificates to haproxy  # noqa: no-handler
   159:       ansible.builtin.command:
   160:         cmd: |
   161:           /home/acme/.acme.sh/acme.sh
   162:             --deploy
   163:             --deploy-hook haproxy
   164:             --domain "{{ item }}"
   165:       environment:
   166:         DEPLOY_HAPROXY_HOT_UPDATE: "yes"
   167:         DEPLOY_HAPROXY_STATS_SOCKET: "/var/lib/haproxy/haproxy.stats"
   168:         DEPLOY_HAPROXY_PEM_PATH: "/etc/haproxy/certs"
   169:       loop: "{{ haproxy_ssl_hosts }}"
   170:       when: "acme_issue.changed"
   171:       register: "result"
   172:       changed_when: "result.changed"
   173:       become_user: "acme"
   174:       become: true

     2: # This role runs all of the tasks needed to make the new code live,
     3: # with handlers to restart nginx and cleanup old deployments.
     4: 
     5: # It assumes the standard configuration /srv/www symlinks to /var/www
     6: # used in CDH Django projects.
     7: ---
     8: - name: Do final configurations and restart webserver
     9:   become: true
    10:   become_user: "{{ deploy_user }}"
    11:   block:
    12:     - name: Create "next" symlink for any final steps before switching live
    13:       ansible.builtin.file:
    14:         src: "{{ deploy }}"
    15:         dest: "{{ install_root }}/next"
    16:         state: link
    17:       tags:
    18:         - never
    19:         - final-pause
    20: 
    21:     - name: pause before switching live
    22:       ansible.builtin.pause:
    23:         prompt: "Do any steps needed before the new version is live, e.g., reindexing. (CTRL-C when done)"
    24:       tags:
    25:         - never
    26:         - final-pause
    27: 
    28:     - name: Remove "next" symlink
    29:       ansible.builtin.file:
    30:         dest: "{{ install_root }}/next"
    31:         state: absent
    32:       tags:
    33:         - never
    34:         - final-pause
    35: 
    36:     - name: Check for "current" symlink; if present, save path
    37:       ansible.builtin.stat:
    38:         path: "{{ install_root }}/current"
    39:       register: previous
    40: 
    41:     - name: Set current symlink

    43:         src: "{{ deploy }}"
    44:         dest: "{{ install_root }}/current"
    45:         state: link
    46: 
    47:     - name: Create "current" symlink for new deploy
    48:       ansible.builtin.stat:
    49:         path: "{{ install_root }}/current"
    50:       register: current
    51: 
    52:     - name: If deploy path differs from last "current", update "previous" symlink
    53:       ansible.builtin.file:
    54:         src: "{{ previous.stat.lnk_target }}"
    55:         dest: "{{ install_root }}/previous"
    56:         state: link
    57:       when:
    58:         - previous.stat.exists | default(false)
    59:         - previous.stat.islnk  | default(false)
    60:         - current.stat.islnk   | default(false)
    61:         - previous.stat.lnk_target is defined
    62:         - current.stat.lnk_target is defined
    63:         - previous.stat.lnk_target != current.stat.lnk_target

source_context:
1: # Check on the webportal's allowance and update if necessary
     2: 
     3: # This task pulls curl docker image from Docker Hub. We use curl docker image
     4: # instead of locally installed curl so that we can run curl command inside sia
     5: # docker network defined later as docker run ... --network="container:sia" ....
     6: - name: Pull curl docker image
     7:   community.docker.docker_image:
     8:     name: "{{ curl_docker_image }}"
     9:     source: pull
    10: 
    11: # Some servers have blocked outgoing traffic to local networks so curl sia from
    12: # host will refuse connection, we have to curl inside docker compose network.
    13: 
    14: # Get the ip address for the sia container
    15: - name: Get sia service IP inside docker compose network
    16:   command: docker inspect -f "{% raw %}{{ range.NetworkSettings.Networks }}{{ .IPAddress }}{{ end }}{% endraw %}" sia
    17:   register: sia_ip_result
    18: 
    19: # Get the renter's information
    20: - name: Grab the Renter's information
    21:   command: docker run --rm --network="container:sia" "{{ curl_docker_image }}" -A "Sia-Agent" "http://{{ sia_ip_result.stdout }}:9980/renter"
    22:   register: renter_get_result
    23: 
    24: - name: Parse the Renter's information as json
    25:   set_fact:
    26:     # Parse the RenterGET json object from stdout response
    27:     renter_json: "{{ renter_get_result.stdout | from_json }}"
    28: 
    29: - name: Get Allowance Funds and Financial Metrics from the Renter's information
    30:   set_fact:
    31:     # Grab the allowance funds
    32:     allowance_funds: "{{ renter_json.settings.allowance.funds }}"
    33:     # Grab the financial metrics and the maintenance spending
    34:     financial_metrics: "{{ renter_json.financialmetrics }}"
    35: 
    36: # This tasks calculates the unspent unallocated based on the calculation in the
    37: # ContractorSpending SpendingBreakdown method from skyd
    38: # https://gitlab.com/SkynetLabs/skyd/-/blob/master/skymodules/renter.go
    39: - name: Calculate Unspent Unallocated and Grab Allowance Funds
    40:   # Determine variables needed for this task
    41:   vars:
    42:     # This is the lower threshold, types.NewCurrency64(10e3)
    43:     unspent_unallocated_lower_threshold: 10000
    44:     # Calculate what 20% of the allowance funds are
    45:     twenty_percent_allowance: "{{ allowance_funds|int / 5 }}"
    46:     maintenance_spending: "{{ financial_metrics.maintenancespending }}"
    47:     # Calculate the total spent
    48:     total_spent: >-
    49:       {{ financial_metrics.contractfees|int +
    50:       financial_metrics.uploadspending|int +
    51:       financial_metrics.downloadspending|int +
    52:       financial_metrics.storagespending|int +
    53:       financial_metrics.fundaccountspending|int +
    54:       maintenance_spending.accountbalancecost|int +
    55:       maintenance_spending.fundaccountcost|int +
    56:       maintenance_spending.updatepricetablecost|int }}
    57:     # Calculate the unspent allocated
    58:     unspent_allocated: "{{ financial_metrics.totalallocated|int - total_spent|int }}"
    59:     # Calculate the unspent unallocated
    60:     unspent_unallocated: "{{ financial_metrics.unspent|int - unspent_allocated|int }}"
    61:   # Define facts needed in the following tasks
    62:   set_fact:
    63:     # See if over 80% of the allowance has been allocated
    64:     eighty_percent_used_update: "{{ twenty_percent_allowance|int > unspent_unallocated|int }}"
    65:     # See if unspent unallocated is below the lower threshold
    66:     below_threshold_update: "{{ unspent_unallocated|int < unspent_unallocated_lower_threshold|int }}"
    67:     # Define the amount the allowance should be updated to
    68:     update_amount: "{{ twenty_percent_allowance|int + allowance_funds|int }}"
    69: 
    70: # If either of the allowance update checks are valid, increase the allowance.
    71: - name: Update Allowance if needed
    72:   # All units are in hastings so H suffix must be used
    73:   ansible.builtin.command: "docker exec sia siac renter setallowance --amount {{ update_amount }}H"
    74:   when: eighty_percent_used_update|bool or below_threshold_update|bool

     7: - name: Regenerate static Docker containers

    16:     # Use a safe delimiter (|||) that cannot appear in any docker ps output field
    17:     - name: Get all aqa_ container details in one pass
    18:       shell: >-
    19:         docker ps --filter "status=running"
    20:         --format "{% raw %}{{.Names}}|||{{.Image}}|||{{.Ports}}{% endraw %}"
    21:         | grep -i 'aqa_'
    22:       register: running_containers_raw
    23:       changed_when: false
    24:       failed_when: false
    25: 
    26:     - name: Build aqa_containers data structure
    27:       vars:
    28:         # Each line: "<name>|||<image>|||<ports>"
    29:         # e.g. "U2404.32001|||aqa_u2404|||0.0.0.0:32001->22/tcp"
    30:         parsed: >-
    31:           {{
    32:             running_containers_raw.stdout_lines
    33:             | map('split', '|||')
    34:             | list
    35:           }}
    36:         # Strip registry prefix, aqa_ prefix, .arm32 suffix, and :tag suffix
    37:         image_suffix: >-
    38:           {{
    39:             item[1] | regex_replace('^(localhost/)?aqa_', '')
    40:                     | regex_replace('\.arm32$', '')
    41:                     | regex_replace(':.*$', '')
    42:           }}
    43:         dockerfile_path: "roles/DockerStatic/Dockerfiles/Dockerfile.{{ image_suffix }}"
    44:         dockerfile_exists: "{{ lookup('first_found', dockerfile_path, errors='ignore') }}"
    45:       set_fact:
    46:         aqa_containers: >-
    47:           {{
    48:             aqa_containers | default([]) + [{
    49:               'name':       item[0],
    50:               'port':       item[0].split('.')[-2] if item[0].upper().endswith('.ARM32')
    51:                             else item[0].split('.')[-1],
    52:               'isArm32':    item[0].upper().endswith('.ARM32'),
    53:               'dockerfile': dockerfile_path if dockerfile_exists else None
    54:             }]
    55:           }}

    57:       when: running_containers_raw.stdout_lines | length > 0

    61:         msg:
    62:           - "name:       {{ item.name }}"

    65:           - "dockerfile: {{ item.dockerfile }}"

source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Blue-green upgrade method: Create publications and slots for logical replication.
     3: 
     4: # One publication (if pg_publication_count = 1)
     5: - block:
     6:     - name: "Create publication for logical replication (database: {{ dbname | default('postgres') }})"
     7:       ansible.builtin.command: >-
     8:         {{ psql_command }} -d {{ dbname }} -tAXc "
     9:         drop publication if exists {{ publication_name }};
    10:         create publication {{ publication_name }} for all tables;"
    11: 
    12:     - name: "Create slot for logical replication (database: {{ dbname | default('postgres') }})"
    13:       ansible.builtin.command: >-
    14:         {{ psql_command }} -d {{ dbname }} -tAXc "
    15:         select pg_drop_replication_slot('{{ slot_name }}')
    16:         from pg_replication_slots where slot_name = '{{ slot_name }}';
    17:         select lsn from pg_create_logical_replication_slot('{{ slot_name }}', 'pgoutput');"
    18:       register: pg_slot_lsn
    19: 
    20:     - name: "Set variable: target_lsn"
    21:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    22:         target_lsn: "{{ pg_slot_lsn.stdout | trim }}"
    23:       when: not reverse_replication | default(false) | bool # skip for reverse replication
    24:   vars:
    25:     publication_name: "{{ pg_publication_name if not reverse_replication | default(false) | bool else pg_reverse_publication_name }}"
    26:     subscription_slot_name: "{{ pg_subscription_slot_name if not reverse_replication | default(false) | bool else pg_reverse_subscription_slot_name }}"
    27:     slot_name: "{{ (subscription_slot_name ~ '_' ~ dbname) | lower | regex_replace('[^a-z0-9_]+', '_') }}"
    28:     publisher_group: "{{ 'target_cluster' if reverse_replication | default(false) | bool else 'source_cluster' }}"
    29:     psql_command: "psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p {{ postgresql_port }} -U {{ patroni_superuser_username }}"
    30:   environment:
    31:     PATH: "{{ ansible_env.PATH }}:{{ pg_new_bindir }}:{{ pg_old_bindir }}"
    32:     PGPASSWORD: "{{ patroni_superuser_password }}"
    33:   when:
    34:     - inventory_hostname in (groups.get(publisher_group, []) | default([], true))
    35:     - patroni_cluster_leader | default(false) | bool
    36:     - pg_publication_count | int == 1
    37: 
    38: # Multiple publications (if pg_publication_count > 1)
    39: - block:
    40:     # Split tables (sorted by DML activity) into groups for publications to evenly distribute tables across slots.
    41:     - name: "Get a list of tables distributed by groups (database: {{ dbname | default('postgres') }})"
    42:       ansible.builtin.shell: |
    43:         {{ psql_command }} -d {{ dbname }} -tAXc "
    44:         do \$$
    45:         declare
    46:           num_groups constant int := {{ pg_publication_count }};
    47:           group_weights bigint[] := array_fill(0, array[num_groups]);
    48:           random_group_index int;
    49:           lowest_weight_index int;
    50:           lowest_weight bigint;
    51:           table_rec record;
    52:         begin
    53:           create temp table tables_groups_tmp (
    54:             group_id int,
    55:             table_name text,
    56:             weight bigint,
    57:             total_weight bigint
    58:           );
    59: 
    60:           for table_rec in
    61:             select
    62:               format('\\\"%I\\\".\\\"%I\\\"', schemaname, relname) as table_name,
    63:               n_tup_ins + n_tup_upd + n_tup_del as weight
    64:             from pg_stat_user_tables
    65:             where relname <> 'tables_groups_tmp'
    66:               and not exists (
    67:                 select 1
    68:                 from pg_class
    69:                 where oid = pg_stat_user_tables.relid
    70:                   and (relkind = 'p' or relid in (select inhparent from pg_inherits))
    71:               )  -- Exclude parent tables for both declarative and inheritance-based partitioning
    72:             order by weight desc
    73:           loop
    74:             -- for tables with a weight > 0, we find the group with the lowest total weight
    75:             if table_rec.weight > 0 then
    76:               lowest_weight_index := 1;
    77:               lowest_weight := group_weights[1];
    78:               for i in 2..num_groups loop
    79:                 if group_weights[i] < lowest_weight then
    80:                   lowest_weight_index := i;
    81:                   lowest_weight := group_weights[i];
    82:                 end if;
    83:               end loop;
    84:             -- for tables with a weight = 0, randomly select a group
    85:             else
    86:               random_group_index := (trunc(random() * num_groups) + 1)::int;
    87:               lowest_weight_index := random_group_index;
    88:             end if;
    89: 
    90:             group_weights[lowest_weight_index] := group_weights[lowest_weight_index] + table_rec.weight;
    91: 
    92:             insert into tables_groups_tmp (group_id, table_name, weight, total_weight)
    93:             values (lowest_weight_index, table_rec.table_name, table_rec.weight, group_weights[lowest_weight_index]);
    94:           end loop;
    95:         end \$$;
    96: 
    97:         -- get lists of tables separated by groups
    98:         select
    99:           string_agg(table_name, ',') as tables
   100:         from tables_groups_tmp
   101:         group by group_id
   102:         order by group_id;"
   103:       args:
   104:         executable: /bin/bash
   105:       register: tables_groups
   106: 
   107:     # Monitor the locks and terminate the backend blocking the 'create publication' query (for more than 10 seconds)
   108:     - name: "Start pg_terminator script: Monitor locks and terminate the 'create publication' blockers"
   109:       ansible.builtin.shell: |
   110:         echo $$ > /tmp/pg_terminator.pid
   111:         for i in {1..360}; do
   112:           {{ psql_command }} -d postgres -tAXc "
   113:           with blocker_pids(pid) as (
   114:             select unnest(pg_blocking_pids(pid))
   115:             from pg_stat_activity
   116:             where
   117:               query ilike '% create publication %'
   118:               and wait_event_type = 'Lock'
   119:           )
   120:           select
   121:             now(),
   122:             pg_terminate_backend(pid),
   123:             pid,
   124:             clock_timestamp() - xact_start as xact_lasted,
   125:             query
   126:           from pg_stat_activity
   127:           where
   128:             pid in (select pid from blocker_pids)
   129:             and xact_start < clock_timestamp() - interval '10s';" >> /tmp/pg_terminator.log
   130:           sleep 10
   131:         done
   132:       args:
   133:         executable: /bin/bash
   134:       async: 3600  # run the command asynchronously, max exec time: 1 hour
   135:       poll: 0
   136: 
   137:     # Create multiple publications (for each table group)
   138:     # Note: ulimit - will increase stack size and ARG_MAX to prevent error 'Argument list too long'
   139:     - name: "Create publications for logical replication (database: {{ dbname | default('postgres') }})"
   140:       ansible.builtin.shell: >-
   141:         ulimit -S -s {{ create_publication_stack_size | default(32768) }};
   142:         {{ psql_command }} -d {{ dbname }} -tAXc "
   143:         drop publication if exists {{ publication_name }}_{{ '%02d' % (idx + 1) }};
   144:         create publication {{ publication_name }}_{{ '%02d' % (idx + 1) }} for table {{ item }};"
   145:       args:
   146:         executable: /bin/bash
   147:       loop: "{{ tables_groups.stdout_lines | reject('equalto', 'DO') | list }}"
   148:       loop_control:
   149:         index_var: idx
   150:         label: "{{ publication_name }}_{{ '%02d' % (idx + 1) }}"
   151: 
   152:     # Create multiple slots (for each publication/subscription)
   153:     - name: "Create slots for logical replication (database: {{ dbname | default('postgres') }})"
   154:       ansible.builtin.command: >-
   155:         {{ psql_command }} -d {{ dbname }} -tAXc "
   156:         select pg_drop_replication_slot('{{ slot_name }}_{{ '%02d' % (idx + 1) }}')
   157:         from pg_replication_slots where slot_name = '{{ slot_name }}_{{ '%02d' % (idx + 1) }}';
   158:         select lsn from pg_create_logical_replication_slot('{{ slot_name }}_{{ '%02d' % (idx + 1) }}', 'pgoutput');"
   159:       register: multiple_pg_slot_lsn
   160:       loop: "{{ range(0, pg_publication_count | int) | list }}"
   161:       loop_control:
   162:         index_var: idx
   163:         label: "{{ slot_name }}_{{ '%02d' % (idx + 1) }}"
   164: 
   165:     - name: "Stop pg_terminator script"
   166:       ansible.builtin.shell: |
   167:         pid=$(cat /tmp/pg_terminator.pid)
   168:         ps -p $pid > /dev/null 2>&1 && kill -9 $pid
   169:       args:
   170:         executable: /bin/bash
   171:       ignore_errors: true
   172: 
   173:     - name: "Set variable: target_lsn"
   174:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   175:         target_lsn: "{{ multiple_pg_slot_lsn['results'][-1]['stdout'] | trim }}"
   176:       when: not reverse_replication | default(false) | bool # skip for reverse replication
   177:   vars:
   178:     publication_name: "{{ pg_publication_name if not reverse_replication | default(false) | bool else pg_reverse_publication_name }}"
   179:     subscription_slot_name: "{{ pg_subscription_slot_name if not reverse_replication | default(false) | bool else pg_reverse_subscription_slot_name }}"
   180:     slot_name: "{{ (subscription_slot_name ~ '_' ~ dbname) | lower | regex_replace('[^a-z0-9_]+', '_') }}"
   181:     publisher_group: "{{ 'target_cluster' if reverse_replication | default(false) | bool else 'source_cluster' }}"
   182:     psql_command: "psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p {{ postgresql_port }} -U {{ patroni_superuser_username }}"
   183:   environment:
   184:     PATH: "{{ ansible_env.PATH }}:{{ pg_new_bindir }}:{{ pg_old_bindir }}"
   185:     PGPASSWORD: "{{ patroni_superuser_password }}"
   186:   when:
   187:     - inventory_hostname in (groups.get(publisher_group, []) | default([], true))
   188:     - patroni_cluster_leader | default(false) | bool
   189:     - pg_publication_count | int > 1

1: ---
     2: #####
     3: # This set of tasks downloads, decompresses, converts and uploads an image to the target cloud
     4: # The "output" of the tasks is a variable containing the image ID
     5: #####
     6: 
     7: - name: Ensure working directory is ready
     8:   when: not community_images_workdir
     9:   block:
    10:     - name: Get temporary working directory
    11:       ansible.builtin.tempfile:
    12:         state: directory
    13:       register: community_images_tempdir
    14: 
    15:     - name: Set working directory fact
    16:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    17:         community_images_workdir: "{{ community_images_tempdir.path }}"
    18: 
    19: - name: Ensure working directory exists
    20:   ansible.builtin.file:
    21:     state: directory
    22:     path: "{{ community_images_workdir }}"
    23:     mode: "0755"
    24: 
    25: - name: "List images with name - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
    26:   ansible.builtin.command: >-
    27:     {{ community_images_openstack_cli_path }}
    28:     image list -f json
    29:     --name {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}
    30:   changed_when: false
    31:   register: community_images_project_image_list_cmd
    32: 
    33: - name: "List images from other projects with name - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
    34:   ansible.builtin.command: >-
    35:     {{ community_images_openstack_cli_path }}
    36:     image list -f json --community
    37:     --name {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}
    38:   changed_when: false
    39:   register: community_images_community_image_list_cmd
    40: 
    41: # Images already in project take precedence over community-visibility images from other projects
    42: - name: "Set image list fact - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
    43:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    44:     community_images_image_list: "{{
    45:                                   _community_images_project_image_list
    46:                                   if _community_images_use_images_in_project
    47:                                   else _community_images_project_image_list
    48:                                   }}"
    49:   changed_when: false
    50:   vars:
    51:     _community_images_project_image_list: "{{ community_images_project_image_list_cmd.stdout | from_json }}"
    52:     _community_images_community_image_list: "{{ community_images_community_image_list_cmd.stdout | from_json }}"
    53:     _community_images_use_images_in_project: _community_images_project_image_list | length > 0 or not community_images_use_existing_trusted_community_images or
    54:       community_images_insecure_skip_glance_verify
    55: 
    56: - name: Verify existing images
    57:   when:
    58:     - not community_images_insecure_skip_glance_verify
    59:     - community_images_image_list | length > 0
    60:     - community_images_image_spec.checksum_sha512 is defined
    61:   block:
    62:     - name: Get Glance checksums
    63:       ansible.builtin.command: >-
    64:         {{ community_images_openstack_cli_path }}
    65:         image show -f json
    66:         {{ _image_id }}
    67:       loop: "{{ community_images_image_list | map(attribute='ID') }}"
    68:       loop_control:
    69:         loop_var: _image_id
    70:       changed_when: false
    71:       register: _community_images_show_cmd
    72: 
    73:     - name: Set glance checksum as fact
    74:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    75:         community_images_glance_checksum_list: "{{
    76:           _community_images_show_cmd.results
    77:           | map(attribute='stdout')
    78:           | map('from_json')
    79:           | map(attribute='properties.os_hash_value')
    80:           }}"
    81: 
    82:     - name: Verify Glance checksums
    83:       vars:
    84:         _community_images_image_spec_glance_checksum: "{{ community_images_image_spec.checksum_sha512.split(':')[1] }}"
    85:       block:
    86:         - name: "Ensure all Glance checksums are the same for images named {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
    87:           ansible.builtin.assert:
    88:             that: "{{ community_images_glance_checksum_list | unique | length == 1 }}"
    89:             fail_msg: |
    90:               Expecting a single image with name {{ community_images_image_spec.name }} and
    91:               os_hash_value {{ _community_images_image_spec_glance_checksum }}, found
    92:               {{ community_images_glance_checksum_list | unique }}. Ensure that duplicate, untrusted images
    93:               are unused and if so remove them with `openstack image delete`, or ensure a new set of trusted, per-project images
    94:               are pulled by setting `community_images_use_existing_trusted_community_images: false`.
    95:         - name: Ensure Glance checksum matches manifest
    96:           ansible.builtin.assert:
    97:             that: _glance_checksum == _community_images_image_spec_glance_checksum
    98:             fail_msg: >-
    99:               Expecting os_hash_value to be sha512 checksum
   100:               {{ _community_images_image_spec_glance_checksum }}, was {{ _glance_checksum }}. Ensure the untrusted image is unused
   101:               and if so remove it with `openstack image delete`. A new set of trusted, per-project images
   102:               are pulled by setting `community_images_use_existing_trusted_community_images: false`.
   103:           vars:
   104:             _glance_checksum: "{{ community_images_glance_checksum_list | first }}"
   105: - name: Get information on existing images from OpenStack
   106:   when: "community_images_image_list | length > 0"
   107:   block:
   108:     - name: "Get ID fact from pre-existing image - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
   109:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   110:         community_images_image_id: "{{ community_images_image_list | map(attribute='ID') | first }}"
   111: 
   112:     - name: "Fetch pre-existing image - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
   113:       ansible.builtin.command: >-
   114:         {{ community_images_openstack_cli_path }}
   115:         image show -f json
   116:         {{ community_images_image_id }}
   117:       changed_when: false
   118:       register: community_images_image_info
   119: 
   120:     - name: "Set visibility fact from pre-existing image - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
   121:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   122:         community_images_image_current_visibility: "{{ community_images_image_info.stdout | from_json | json_query('visibility') }}"
   123: 
   124: - name: Download, convert and upload images to Glance
   125:   when: "community_images_image_list | length == 0"
   126:   block:
   127:     - name: "Set image facts - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
   128:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   129:         community_images_image_download_path: >-
   130:           {{ (community_images_workdir, community_images_image_spec.name + '.download') | path_join }}
   131:         community_images_image_decompress_path: >-
   132:           {{ (community_images_workdir, community_images_image_spec.name + '.decompress') | path_join }}
   133:         community_images_image_convert_path: >-
   134:           {{ (community_images_workdir, community_images_image_spec.name + '.convert') | path_join }}
   135:         community_images_image_decompression_required: >-
   136:           {{ community_images_image_spec.source_url.split('.')[-1] in ['bz2'] }}
   137: 
   138:     - name: "Set image facts (2) - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
   139:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   140:         community_images_image_convert_in_path: >-
   141:           {{-
   142:             community_images_image_decompress_path
   143:             if community_images_image_decompression_required
   144:             else community_images_image_download_path
   145:           }}
   146: 
   147:     - name: "Set image facts (3) - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
   148:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   149:         community_images_image_upload_in_path: >-
   150:           {{-
   151:             community_images_image_convert_in_path
   152:             if community_images_image_spec.source_disk_format == community_images_disk_format
   153:             else community_images_image_convert_path
   154:           }}
   155: 
   156:     - name: "Download image - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
   157:       ansible.builtin.get_url:
   158:         url: "{{ community_images_image_spec.source_url }}"
   159:         dest: "{{ community_images_image_download_path }}"
   160:         checksum: "{{ community_images_image_spec.checksum | default(omit) }}"
   161:         timeout: 600
   162:         mode: "0644"
   163: 
   164:     - name: "Uncompress image (bzip2) - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
   165:       ansible.builtin.shell: "bunzip2 -dc {{ community_images_image_download_path }} > {{ community_images_image_decompress_path }}"
   166:       args:
   167:         creates: "{{ community_images_image_decompress_path }}"
   168:       when: community_images_image_spec.source_url.endswith('bz2')
   169: 
   170:     - name: "Convert image - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
   171:       ansible.builtin.command: >-
   172:         qemu-img convert
   173:           -f {{ community_images_image_spec.source_disk_format }}
   174:           -O {{ community_images_disk_format }}
   175:           "{{ community_images_image_convert_in_path }}"
   176:           "{{ community_images_image_convert_path }}"
   177:       args:
   178:         creates: "{{ community_images_image_convert_path }}"
   179:       when: community_images_image_spec.source_disk_format != community_images_disk_format
   180: 
   181:     # openstack.cloud.image is currently broken due to JSON processing code
   182:     # https://storyboard.openstack.org/#!/story/2008740
   183:     # Instead, we use the OpenStack CLI directly
   184:     - name: "Upload image - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
   185:       ansible.builtin.command: >-
   186:         {{ community_images_openstack_cli_path }} image create
   187:           -f json
   188:           --container-format {{ community_images_image_spec.container_format }}
   189:           --disk-format {{ community_images_disk_format }}
   190:           --file {{ community_images_image_upload_in_path }}
   191:           {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}
   192:       register: community_images_create_image_cmd
   193:       changed_when: true
   194: 
   195:     - name: "Clean up files - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
   196:       ansible.builtin.file:
   197:         path: "{{ path }}"
   198:         state: absent
   199:       loop:
   200:         - "{{ community_images_image_download_path }}"
   201:         - "{{ community_images_image_decompress_path }}"
   202:         - "{{ community_images_image_convert_path }}"
   203:       loop_control:
   204:         loop_var: path
   205: 
   206:     - name: "Set image ID fact - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
   207:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   208:         community_images_image_id: "{{ community_images_create_image_cmd.stdout | from_json | json_query('id') }}"
   209:         community_images_image_current_visibility: "{{ community_images_create_image_cmd.stdout | from_json | json_query('visibility') }}"
   210: 
   211: - name: "Set image visibility fact - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
   212:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   213:     community_images_image_visibility: >-
   214:       {{-
   215:         community_images_image_spec.get('visibility', community_images_default_visibility)
   216:         if community_images_update_existing_visibility
   217:         else community_images_image_current_visibility
   218:       }}
   219: 
   220: - name: "Set image visibility - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
   221:   ansible.builtin.command: >-
   222:     {{ community_images_openstack_cli_path }}
   223:     image set
   224:     --{{ community_images_image_visibility }}
   225:     {{ community_images_image_id }}
   226:   when: community_images_image_visibility != community_images_image_current_visibility
   227:   changed_when: true
   228: 
   229: 
   230:   # Keeping this task allows us to set properties on images that already exist, rather than just at upload time.
   231: - name: "Set custom properties for image - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
   232:   ansible.builtin.command: >-
   233:     {{ community_images_openstack_cli_path }}
   234:       image set
   235:       {%- for property in (community_images_image_spec.properties | default([])) + community_images_custom_properties %}
   236:       --property {{ property | quote }}
   237:       {%- endfor %}
   238:       {{ community_images_image_id }}
   239:   when: "((community_images_image_spec.properties | default([])) + community_images_custom_properties) | length > 0"
   240:   changed_when: true
   241: 
   242: - name: Share and accept images with OpenStack projects
   243:   when: "community_images_image_visibility == 'shared'"
   244:   block:
   245:     - name: "Share image with project - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
   246:       ansible.builtin.command: >-
   247:         {{ community_images_openstack_cli_path }}
   248:         image add project
   249:         {{ community_images_image_id }} {{ project_id }}
   250:       register: community_images_image_add_project
   251:       changed_when: community_images_image_add_project.rc == 0
   252:       failed_when: >-
   253:         community_images_image_add_project.rc != 0 and
   254:         not community_images_image_add_project.stderr.startswith("ConflictException")
   255:       loop: "{{ community_images_share_projects | map(attribute='id') | list }}"
   256:       loop_control:
   257:         loop_var: project_id
   258: 
   259:     - name: "Accept image into project - {{ community_images_image_spec.name }}"
   260:       ansible.builtin.command: >-
   261:         {{ community_images_openstack_cli_path }}
   262:         image set
   263:         --accept {{ community_images_image_id }}
   264:       environment:
   265:         OS_CLOUD: "{{ project_key }}"
   266:       loop: "{{ community_images_share_projects | map(attribute='key') | list }}"
   267:       loop_control:
   268:         loop_var: project_key
   269:       changed_when: true

    53: #
    54: # Note we disable the no-changed-when check for ansible-lint because a
    55: # provisioner rerun should update GPG key information.
    56: #
    57: 
    58: # The --batch flag makes sure that gpg2 doesn't attempt to do anything
    59: # interactive.
    60: - name: Import gpg keys
    61:   ansible.builtin.shell:
    62:     cmd: >-
    63:       set -o pipefail

    74:     - "{{ cyhy_feeds_public_gpg_key }}"

    79: - name: Import gpg trust
    80:   # The value stored in the Parameter Store has a newline so we trim the value
    81:   # before quoting. A quoted newline causes a failure when gpg2 attempts to
    82:   # import the owner trust.
    83:   ansible.builtin.shell:
    84:     cmd: >-
    85:       set -o pipefail

   101: # resulted in documents being updated and their modification time being updated
   102: # to fall past the end of the query cutoff. Changes were made to the script in

   104: # https://github.com/cisagov/cyhy-feeds/pull/37
   105: #

   112:       python3 /var/cyhy/scripts/cyhy-feeds/cyhy-data-extract.py

   114:       --scan-config /var/cyhy/scripts/cyhy-feeds/scan_reader.yml

   119:       | /usr/bin/logger --tag cyhy-feeds
   120:     minute: "0"
   121:     name: Nightly cyhy extract

source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Mailu mail server deployment (consolidated on www with nginx-proxy)
     3: 
     4: - name: Create Mailu directory
     5:   become: true
     6:   ansible.builtin.file:
     7:     path: "{{ mailu_install_path }}"
     8:     state: directory
     9:     mode: "755"
    10: 
    11: - name: Create Mailu data directories
    12:   become: true
    13:   ansible.builtin.file:
    14:     path: "{{ mailu_install_path }}/{{ item }}"
    15:     state: directory
    16:     mode: "755"
    17:   loop:
    18:     - data
    19:     - dkim
    20:     - mail
    21:     - overrides
    22:     - overrides/nginx
    23:     - overrides/dovecot
    24:     - overrides/postfix
    25:     - overrides/rspamd
    26:     - overrides/roundcube
    27:     - redis
    28:     - webmail
    29:     - filter
    30:     - mailqueue
    31: 
    32: - name: Deploy mailu.env
    33:   become: true
    34:   ansible.builtin.template:
    35:     src: mailu.env.j2
    36:     dest: "{{ mailu_install_path }}/mailu.env"
    37:     mode: "600"
    38:   notify: Restart Mailu
    39: 
    40: - name: Deploy docker-compose.yml
    41:   become: true
    42:   ansible.builtin.template:
    43:     src: docker-compose.yml.j2
    44:     dest: "{{ mailu_install_path }}/docker-compose.yml"
    45:     mode: "644"
    46:   notify: Restart Mailu
    47: 
    48: # nginx-proxy stores certs as <domain>.crt/<domain>.key
    49: # Mailu expects cert.pem/key.pem - create symlinks
    50: - name: Create cert.pem symlink for Mailu
    51:   become: true
    52:   ansible.builtin.file:
    53:     src: "{{ mailu_hostname }}.crt"
    54:     dest: /var/lib/docker/volumes/certs/_data/cert.pem
    55:     state: link
    56:     force: true
    57: 
    58: - name: Create key.pem symlink for Mailu
    59:   become: true
    60:   ansible.builtin.file:
    61:     src: "{{ mailu_hostname }}.key"
    62:     dest: /var/lib/docker/volumes/certs/_data/key.pem
    63:     state: link
    64:     force: true
    65: 
    66: - name: Start Mailu stack
    67:   become: true
    68:   community.docker.docker_compose_v2:
    69:     project_src: "{{ mailu_install_path }}"
    70:     state: present
    71:     pull: always
    72: 
    73: - name: Wait for Mailu to be ready
    74:   become: true
    75:   ansible.builtin.wait_for:
    76:     port: 443 # nginx-proxy handles HTTPS
    77:     delay: 10
    78:     timeout: 120
    79: 
    80: - name: Create admin user
    81:   become: true
    82:   ansible.builtin.command:
    83:     cmd: >
    84:       docker compose exec -T admin flask mailu admin
    85:       {{ mailu_admin_user }} {{ mailu_domain }} {{ mailu_admin_password }}
    86:   args:
    87:     chdir: "{{ mailu_install_path }}"
    88:   register: mailu_admin_result
    89:   changed_when: "'created' in mailu_admin_result.stdout"
    90:   failed_when: false # May fail if user exists
    91:   no_log: true # Hide admin password
    92: 
    93: - name: Create mail users
    94:   become: true
    95:   ansible.builtin.command:
    96:     cmd: >
    97:       docker compose exec -T admin flask mailu user
    98:       {{ item.user }} {{ mailu_domain }} {{ item.password }}
    99:   args:
   100:     chdir: "{{ mailu_install_path }}"
   101:   loop: "{{ mailu_users }}"
   102:   register: mailu_user_result
   103:   changed_when: false # Can't reliably detect from looped command
   104:   failed_when: false # May fail if user exists
   105:   no_log: true # Hide passwords
   106: 
   107: # These DKIM tasks loop over domain NAMES, not the mailu_additional_domains
   108: # entries themselves. The entries nest user passwords, and Ansible echoes the
   109: # loop item for every skipped or registered result - which printed live
   110: # mailbox credentials in plaintext. Looping over names keeps secrets out of
   111: # the output without needing no_log, which would also hide the DKIM keys these
   112: # tasks exist to surface.
   113: - name: Check if additional domain DKIM key exists
   114:   become: true
   115:   ansible.builtin.stat:
   116:     path: "{{ mailu_install_path }}/dkim/{{ item }}.dkim.key"
   117:   loop: "{{ mailu_additional_domains | default([]) | map(attribute='domain') | list }}"
   118:   register: mailu_additional_dkim_stat
   119: 
   120: - name: Import additional domains with DKIM key generation (first time only)
   121:   become: true
   122:   ansible.builtin.shell:
   123:     cmd: |
   124:       set -o pipefail
   125:       echo 'domain:
   126:         - name: {{ item.item }}
   127:           dkim_key: -generate-
   128:       ' | docker compose exec -T admin flask mailu config-import --update
   129:   args:
   130:     chdir: "{{ mailu_install_path }}"
   131:     executable: /bin/bash
   132:   loop: "{{ mailu_additional_dkim_stat.results | default([]) }}"
   133:   when: not item.stat.exists
   134:   register: mailu_domain_result_new
   135:   changed_when: "'updated' in mailu_domain_result_new.stdout | default('')"
   136:   failed_when: false
   137: 
   138: - name: Import additional domains without regenerating DKIM key
   139:   become: true
   140:   ansible.builtin.shell:
   141:     cmd: |
   142:       set -o pipefail
   143:       echo 'domain:
   144:         - name: {{ item.item }}
   145:       ' | docker compose exec -T admin flask mailu config-import --update
   146:   args:
   147:     chdir: "{{ mailu_install_path }}"
   148:     executable: /bin/bash
   149:   loop: "{{ mailu_additional_dkim_stat.results | default([]) }}"
   150:   when: item.stat.exists
   151:   register: mailu_domain_result_existing
   152:   changed_when: "'updated' in mailu_domain_result_existing.stdout | default('')"
   153:   failed_when: false
   154: 
   155: - name: Create additional domain users
   156:   become: true
   157:   ansible.builtin.command:
   158:     cmd: >
   159:       docker compose exec -T admin flask mailu user
   160:       {{ item.1.user }} {{ item.0.domain }} {{ item.1.password }}
   161:   args:
   162:     chdir: "{{ mailu_install_path }}"
   163:   loop: "{{ mailu_additional_domains | default([]) | subelements('users') }}"
   164:   register: mailu_user_result
   165:   changed_when: false
   166:   failed_when: false # May fail if user exists
   167:   no_log: true # Hide passwords
   168: 
   169: - name: Create mail aliases
   170:   become: true
   171:   ansible.builtin.command:
   172:     cmd: >
   173:       docker compose exec -T admin flask mailu alias
   174:       {{ item.local }} {{ item.domain }} {{ item.destination }}
   175:   args:
   176:     chdir: "{{ mailu_install_path }}"
   177:   loop: "{{ mailu_aliases | default([]) }}"
   178:   register: mailu_alias_result
   179:   changed_when: false # Can't reliably detect from looped command
   180:   failed_when: false # May fail if alias exists
   181:   # No no_log here, unlike the user-creation tasks above: local/domain/destination
   182:   # are an alias routing rule, not a credential - nothing here is a secret worth
   183:   # hiding from the run output.
   184: 
   185: # `<domain>.dkim.key` is the PRIVATE key. These tasks used to cat it and print
   186: # the result labelled "add this to DNS", which both leaked the signing key to
   187: # stdout/CI logs and was useless as a DNS value. Derive the public half
   188: # instead - that is what belongs in the TXT record.
   189: - name: Get DKIM public key
   190:   become: true
   191:   ansible.builtin.shell:
   192:     cmd: >
   193:       set -o pipefail &&
   194:       openssl rsa -in "{{ mailu_install_path }}/dkim/{{ mailu_domain }}.dkim.key"
   195:       -pubout -outform DER 2>/dev/null | base64 -w0
   196:   args:
   197:     executable: /bin/bash
   198:   register: mailu_dkim_key
   199:   changed_when: false
   200:   failed_when: false
   201: 
   202: - name: Display DKIM key for DNS
   203:   ansible.builtin.debug:
   204:     msg: |
   205:       Add this DKIM record to DNS:
   206:       Name: dkim._domainkey.{{ mailu_domain }}
   207:       Type: TXT
   208:       Value: v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p={{ mailu_dkim_key.stdout | trim }}
   209:   when: mailu_dkim_key.stdout | default('') | trim | length > 0
   210: 
   211: # The lookup above sets failed_when: false, so a missing key or an openssl failure is
   212: # silent. Without this, "no key yet" and "key printed fine" look identical in the run
   213: # output — on a role whose entire purpose here is surfacing the record an operator has
   214: # to paste into DNS. Say so explicitly rather than skipping quietly.
   215: - name: Report that the DKIM key is not available yet
   216:   ansible.builtin.debug:
   217:     msg: >-
   218:       No DKIM public key could be read for {{ mailu_domain }}
   219:       ({{ mailu_install_path }}/dkim/{{ mailu_domain }}.dkim.key).
   220:       Mailu generates it on first start of the admin container, so this is expected on a
   221:       fresh install — re-run this play once it is up to get the DNS record.
   222:   when: mailu_dkim_key.stdout | default('') | trim | length == 0
   223: 
   224: - name: Get DKIM public keys for additional domains
   225:   become: true
   226:   ansible.builtin.shell:
   227:     cmd: >
   228:       set -o pipefail &&
   229:       openssl rsa -in "{{ mailu_install_path }}/dkim/{{ item }}.dkim.key"
   230:       -pubout -outform DER 2>/dev/null | base64 -w0
   231:   args:
   232:     executable: /bin/bash
   233:   loop: "{{ mailu_additional_domains | default([]) | map(attribute='domain') | list }}"
   234:   register: mailu_additional_dkim_keys
   235:   changed_when: false
   236:   failed_when: false
   237: 
   238: - name: Display DKIM keys for additional domains
   239:   ansible.builtin.debug:
   240:     msg: |
   241:       Add this DKIM record to DNS:
   242:       Name: dkim._domainkey.{{ item.item }}
   243:       Type: TXT
   244:       Value: v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p={{ item.stdout | trim }}
   245:   loop: "{{ mailu_additional_dkim_keys.results | default([]) }}"
   246:   loop_control:
   247:     label: "{{ item.item }}"
   248:   when: item.stdout | default('') | trim | length > 0
   249: 
   250: # Same reasoning as the primary domain: silence must not be mistaken for success.
   251: # loop_control.label keeps the loop output to the domain name — the item here is a
   252: # command result, and printing it whole is how this role leaked secrets before.
   253: - name: Report additional domains whose DKIM key is not available yet
   254:   ansible.builtin.debug:
   255:     msg: >-
   256:       No DKIM public key could be read for {{ item.item }}. Mailu generates it on first
   257:       start of the admin container — re-run this play once it is up.
   258:   loop: "{{ mailu_additional_dkim_keys.results | default([]) }}"
   259:   loop_control:
   260:     label: "{{ item.item }}"
   261:   when: item.stdout | default('') | trim | length == 0
   262: 
   263: # --- Nightly mailu -> nas backup (issue #479) ------------------------------
   264: #
   265: # dkim keys, admin sqlite db, mailboxes, and mailu.env - the parts the April
   266: # server wipe permanently lost. Same pipeline shape as goblog-backup
   267: # (jasonernst_com role): sqlite snapshot + additive rsync to the nas' rsync
   268: # daemon over the tailnet. The nas-side prune cron for the db snapshots
   269: # lives in rustd_backup_nas (nas.yml).
   270: - name: Ensure sqlite3 and rsync are installed
   271:   tags: backup
   272:   become: true
   273:   ansible.builtin.apt:
   274:     name: [sqlite3, rsync]
   275:     state: present
   276: 
   277: - name: Create mailu backup directory
   278:   tags: backup
   279:   become: true

   281:     path: "{{ mailu_backup_local_dir }}"

   283:     mode: "700"
   284:     owner: root
   285:     group: root
   286: 
   287: - name: Write the nas rsync-daemon password file

   291:     dest: "{{ mailu_backup_rsync_password_file }}"

   293:     owner: root
   294:     group: root
   295:     mode: "0600"
   296:   no_log: true
   297: 
   298: - name: Deploy the backup script
   299:   tags: backup
   300:   become: true
   301:   ansible.builtin.template:
   302:     src: mailu-backup.sh.j2
   303:     dest: "{{ mailu_install_path }}/mailu-backup.sh"
   304:     mode: "0700"
   305: 
   306: - name: Deploy the backup systemd service
   307:   tags: backup

   309:   ansible.builtin.template:
   310:     src: mailu-backup.service.j2
   311:     dest: /etc/systemd/system/mailu-backup.service
   312:     mode: "0644"

   318:     src: mailu-backup.timer.j2

1: ---
     2: # This task ensures consistency between SSL mutual authentication and client authentication variables
     3: # across different components (Kafka, Schema Registry, Kafka Connect, etc.)
     4: # and across different listeners in Kafka brokers.
     5: # Rules:
     6: # 1. If ssl_client_authentication is 'required' or 'requested', then ssl_mutual_auth_enabled must be true
     7: # 2. If ssl_mutual_auth_enabled is true and ssl_client_authentication is not defined/none, then ssl_client_authentication must be 'required'
     8: #
     9: # To disable mutual TLS (mTLS) for any component of default kafka listener, both variables must be set:
    10: # - <component>_ssl_mutual_auth_enabled = false
    11: # - <component>_ssl_client_authentication = 'none'
    12: 
    13: - name: Define component SSL variable pairs
    14:   set_fact:
    15:     mtls_client_auth_pairs:
    16:       - mutual_auth_var: ssl_mutual_auth_enabled
    17:         client_auth_var: ssl_client_authentication
    18:       - mutual_auth_var: kafka_controller_ssl_mutual_auth_enabled
    19:         client_auth_var: kafka_controller_ssl_client_authentication
    20:       - mutual_auth_var: schema_registry_ssl_mutual_auth_enabled
    21:         client_auth_var: schema_registry_ssl_client_authentication
    22:       - mutual_auth_var: kafka_connect_ssl_mutual_auth_enabled
    23:         client_auth_var: kafka_connect_ssl_client_authentication
    24:       - mutual_auth_var: kafka_rest_ssl_mutual_auth_enabled
    25:         client_auth_var: kafka_rest_ssl_client_authentication
    26:       - mutual_auth_var: kafka_connect_replicator_ssl_mutual_auth_enabled
    27:         client_auth_var: kafka_connect_replicator_ssl_client_authentication
    28: 
    29: - name: Define ssl_mutual_auth_enabled variables
    30:   set_fact:
    31:     "{{ item.mutual_auth_var }}": true
    32:   loop: "{{ mtls_client_auth_pairs }}"
    33:   when:
    34:     - lookup('vars', item.client_auth_var) in ['required','requested']
    35:     - not lookup('vars', item.mutual_auth_var)|bool
    36:   register: mutual_auth_result
    37: 
    38: - name: Define ssl_client_authentication variables
    39:   set_fact:
    40:     "{{ item.client_auth_var }}": required
    41:   loop: "{{ mtls_client_auth_pairs }}"
    42:   when:
    43:     - lookup('vars', item.mutual_auth_var)|bool
    44:     - lookup('vars', item.client_auth_var) == 'none'
    45: 
    46: # These are set for default listeners but not for custom listeners.
    47: # So in order to make custom listeners' mTLS variables consistent we must define them
    48: - name: Set default values for mTLS vars in Kafka broker listeners
    49:   set_fact:
    50:     kafka_broker_listeners: >-
    51:       {{ kafka_broker_listeners | combine({listener_name: kafka_broker_listeners[listener_name] | combine({
    52:         'ssl_mutual_auth_enabled': kafka_broker_listeners[listener_name].ssl_mutual_auth_enabled | default(ssl_mutual_auth_enabled),
    53:         'ssl_client_authentication': kafka_broker_listeners[listener_name].ssl_client_authentication | default(ssl_client_authentication)
    54:       })}) }}
    55:   loop: "{{ kafka_broker_listeners.keys() | list }}"
    56:   loop_control:
    57:     loop_var: listener_name
    58:   when: kafka_broker_listeners is defined
    59: 
    60: - name: Update SSL mutual authentication in Kafka broker listeners
    61:   set_fact:
    62:     kafka_broker_listeners: "{{ kafka_broker_listeners | combine({listener_name: kafka_broker_listeners[listener_name] | combine({'ssl_mutual_auth_enabled': true})}) }}"
    63:   loop: "{{ kafka_broker_listeners.keys() | list }}"
    64:   loop_control:
    65:     loop_var: listener_name
    66:   when:
    67:     - kafka_broker_listeners is defined
    68:     - kafka_broker_listeners[listener_name].ssl_client_authentication in ['required', 'requested']
    69:     - not kafka_broker_listeners[listener_name].ssl_mutual_auth_enabled | bool
    70: 
    71: - name: Update SSL client authentication in Kafka broker listeners
    72:   set_fact:
    73:     kafka_broker_listeners: "{{ kafka_broker_listeners | combine({listener_name: kafka_broker_listeners[listener_name] | combine({'ssl_client_authentication': 'required'})}) }}"
    74:   loop: "{{ kafka_broker_listeners.keys() | list }}"
    75:   loop_control:
    76:     loop_var: listener_name
    77:   when:
    78:     - kafka_broker_listeners is defined
    79:     - kafka_broker_listeners[listener_name].ssl_mutual_auth_enabled | bool
    80:     - kafka_broker_listeners[listener_name].ssl_client_authentication == 'none'
    81: 
    82: - name: Define single listener SSL variable pairs
    83:   set_fact:
    84:     single_listener_mtls_pairs:
    85:       - listener_var: mds_broker_listener
    86:         default_mutual_auth: "{{ ssl_mutual_auth_enabled }}"
    87:         default_client_auth: "{{ ssl_client_authentication }}"
    88:       - listener_var: audit_logs_destination_listener
    89:         default_mutual_auth: "{{ ssl_mutual_auth_enabled }}"
    90:         default_client_auth: "{{ ssl_client_authentication }}"
    91: 
    92: - name: Set default values for SSL fields in single listeners
    93:   set_fact:
    94:     "{{ item.listener_var }}": >-
    95:       {{ lookup('vars', item.listener_var) | combine({
    96:         'ssl_mutual_auth_enabled': lookup('vars', item.listener_var).ssl_mutual_auth_enabled | default(item.default_mutual_auth),
    97:         'ssl_client_authentication': lookup('vars', item.listener_var).ssl_client_authentication | default(item.default_client_auth)
    98:       }) }}
    99:   loop: "{{ single_listener_mtls_pairs }}"
   100:   when: lookup('vars', item.listener_var, default=None) is not none
   101: 
   102: - name: Update SSL mutual authentication in single listeners
   103:   set_fact:
   104:     "{{ item.listener_var }}": "{{ lookup('vars', item.listener_var) | combine({'ssl_mutual_auth_enabled': true}) }}"
   105:   loop: "{{ single_listener_mtls_pairs }}"
   106:   when:
   107:     - lookup('vars', item.listener_var, default=None) is not none
   108:     - lookup('vars', item.listener_var).ssl_client_authentication in ['required', 'requested']
   109:     - not lookup('vars', item.listener_var).ssl_mutual_auth_enabled | bool
   110: 
   111: - name: Update SSL client authentication in single listeners
   112:   set_fact:
   113:     "{{ item.listener_var }}": "{{ lookup('vars', item.listener_var) | combine({'ssl_client_authentication': 'required'}) }}"
   114:   loop: "{{ single_listener_mtls_pairs }}"
   115:   when:
   116:     - lookup('vars', item.listener_var, default=None) is not none
   117:     - lookup('vars', item.listener_var).ssl_mutual_auth_enabled | bool
   118:     - lookup('vars', item.listener_var).ssl_client_authentication == 'none'
