source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Keep internal networks reachable from a VDI guest that runs a VPN client.
     3: #
     4: # A full-tunnel client (FortiClient, and every other one) installs its own
     5: # default route when it connects. From that moment the guest's REPLY packets to
     6: # anything off its own subnet leave through the tunnel and never arrive: an
     7: # established RDP session drops, and every subsequent WinRM converge fails,
     8: # because inbound still reaches the guest while the return path is gone.
     9: #
    10: # A more-specific persistent route per preserved subnet outranks the tunnel's
    11: # default route — including the two-half variant clients often install instead
    12: # of a literal default — so those networks stay on the LAN and everything else
    13: # still goes to the VPN.
    14: #
    15: # Deliberately NOT every private range: a corporate network behind the VPN very
    16: # often overlaps the estate's own private space, and routing that past the
    17: # tunnel would break the resource the VDI exists to reach. Only the subnets
    18: # named by vdi_preserved_vlans move.
    19: 
    20: - name: Fail when the split-tunnel inputs are missing
    21:   # An empty list here is the silent-no-op shape this repo keeps getting bitten
    22:   # by: the play goes green, the operator believes the standard is applied, and
    23:   # the guest drops off the network the next time the VPN connects. A guest in
    24:   # vdi_group has asked for this standard, so absent inputs are a broken
    25:   # inventory, not an opt-out.
    26:   ansible.builtin.assert:
    27:     that:
    28:       - vdi_local_routes_destinations | length > 0
    29:       - vdi_local_routes_gateway | length > 0
    30:     fail_msg: >-
    31:       {{ inventory_hostname }} is in vdi_group but the published inventory
    32:       carries no split-tunnel inputs (destinations:
    33:       {{ vdi_local_routes_destinations | length }}, gateway present:
    34:       {{ vdi_local_routes_gateway | length > 0 }}). Set vdi_preserved_vlans in
    35:       deployment.json and re-run the tofu-proxmox workspace so the inventory
    36:       republishes with vdi_preserved_cidrs and a per-VM gateway.
    37: 
    38: - name: Pin the preserved subnets to the LAN gateway
    39:   # Both policy stores, deliberately. ActiveStore takes effect now; only
    40:   # PersistentStore survives a reboot, and a route that vanishes on the next
    41:   # restart is worse than none — it works when tested and fails unattended.
    42:   # A route whose next hop no longer matches the published gateway is replaced
    43:   # rather than left alongside, so a VLAN renumber converges instead of
    44:   # accumulating a dead entry that still wins on prefix length.
    45:   #
    46:   # win_powershell, not win_shell: win_shell is free-form, so Ansible splits the
    47:   # script as module arguments and this one does not survive it ("unbalanced
    48:   # jinja2 block or quotes" — caught by ansible-lint). Passing the values as
    49:   # typed parameters also keeps Jinja out of the PowerShell entirely.
    50:   ansible.windows.win_powershell:
    51:     parameters:
    52:       Destination: "{{ item }}"
    53:       Gateway: "{{ vdi_local_routes_gateway }}"
    54:       Metric: "{{ vdi_local_routes_metric }}"
    55:     script: |
    56:       param([string]$Destination, [string]$Gateway, [int]$Metric)
    57:       $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
    58: 
    59:       # Resolve the interface that actually reaches the gateway. The gateway sits
    60:       # on the guest's own subnet, which stays on-link even with the tunnel up,
    61:       # so this returns the physical NIC rather than the VPN adapter.
    62:       $ifIndex = (Find-NetRoute -RemoteIPAddress $Gateway -ErrorAction Stop |
    63:                   Select-Object -First 1).InterfaceIndex
    64: 
    65:       # `route -p add`, not New-NetRoute -PolicyStore PersistentStore. The
    66:       # cmdlet rejects the persistent store on this build with "Invalid
    67:       # parameter PolicyStore PersistentStore" (Windows System Error 87) using
    68:       # EITHER -InterfaceIndex or -InterfaceAlias — both were tried against a
    69:       # live guest. Its index form DOES succeed against ActiveStore, which is
    70:       # the dangerous shape: the live route is written, the persistent write
    71:       # errors, and the route disappears at the next reboot. That is precisely
    72:       # the failure this role exists to prevent, and it would read as working.
    73:       #
    74:       # route.exe -p writes the live route AND the registry persistent route in
    75:       # one operation, so the two cannot diverge.
    76:       $parts = $Destination -split '/'
    77:       $network = $parts[0]
    78:       $len = [int]$parts[1]
    79:       $octets = @(0, 0, 0, 0)
    80:       for ($i = 0; $i -lt 4; $i++) {
    81:         $bits = [Math]::Min(8, [Math]::Max(0, $len - ($i * 8)))
    82:         $octets[$i] = [byte](256 - [Math]::Pow(2, 8 - $bits))
    83:       }
    84:       $mask = $octets -join '.'
    85: 
    86:       $live = @(Get-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix $Destination -PolicyStore ActiveStore `
    87:                              -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    88:                 Where-Object { $_.NextHop -eq $Gateway })
    89:       # Check the POLICY STORE, not the legacy
    90:       # Tcpip\Parameters\PersistentRoutes registry key. `route -p add` on this
    91:       # build records the route in PersistentStore and leaves that key empty, so
    92:       # testing the registry finds nothing every time and the task re-adds an
    93:       # already-correct route and reports changed on every converge — verified
    94:       # against the live guest, where the routes were present in the store while
    95:       # the key held nothing at all.
    96:       $persisted = @(Get-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix $Destination `
    97:                                   -PolicyStore PersistentStore `
    98:                                   -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    99:                      Where-Object { $_.NextHop -eq $Gateway })
   100: 
   101:       $changed = $false
   102:       if (-not $live -or -not $persisted) {
   103:         # Clear any stale entry for this prefix first: a route to the same
   104:         # destination via a dead next hop still wins on prefix length and would
   105:         # black-hole the traffic this role is protecting.
   106:         # route.exe writes "Element not found" to STDERR when there is nothing
   107:         # to delete, and with ErrorActionPreference = Stop PowerShell promotes
   108:         # any native stderr to a terminating NativeCommandError — so the
   109:         # clean-up step fails the task in the ordinary case where the route was
   110:         # simply absent. Nothing to delete is a success here, so drop the
   111:         # preference for exactly this call.
   112:         $prev = $ErrorActionPreference
   113:         $ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
   114:         & route delete $network mask $mask 2>&1 | Out-Null
   115:         $ErrorActionPreference = $prev
   116: 
   117:         $out = & route -p add $network mask $mask $Gateway metric $Metric if $ifIndex 2>&1
   118:         if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "route -p add failed (rc=$LASTEXITCODE): $out" }
   119:         $changed = $true
   120:       }
   121: 
   122:       # win_powershell reports changed unless told otherwise, so a converge that
   123:       # altered nothing would still read as a change on every run.
   124:       $Ansible.Changed = $changed
   125:   loop: "{{ vdi_local_routes_destinations }}"

name: roles/dashboard_catalog/tasks/main.yml
review_question: Would an Ansible expert judge this playbook or task file as needing abstraction because it contains too many direct leaf tasks?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Export `dashboard_catalog` — one entry per fronted service — for the board
     3: # roles to render. See defaults/main.yml for why this is built exactly once.
     4: #
     5: # The accumulate-in-a-loop shape mirrors the traefik role's own route
     6: # normalisation, which is the proven idiom in this repo for turning the ingress
     7: # table into a rendered structure.
     8: 
     9: - name: Assert the ingress table and the base domain both resolved
    10:   ansible.builtin.assert:
    11:     that:
    12:       - dashboard_catalog_ingress | length > 0
    13:       - dashboard_catalog_base_domain | trim | length > 0
    14:     fail_msg: >-
    15:       No ingress routes, or PROXMOX_SUBDOMAIN is unset. Rendering a board from
    16:       an empty catalog SUCCEEDS and publishes an empty dashboard, which is
    17:       indistinguishable from a healthy converge — fail here instead.
    18:     quiet: true
    19: 
    20: - name: Build the dashboard catalog from the ingress table
    21:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    22:     dashboard_catalog_services: >-
    23:       {{
    24:         dashboard_catalog_services | default([]) + [{
    25:           'name': item.name,
    26:           'group': item.group | default('other', true),
    27:           'sso': item.sso | default(true),
    28:           'ui': item.ui | default(true),
    29:           'section': item.section | default(none),
    30:           'desc': item.desc | default('', true),
    31:           'fqdn': _fqdn,
    32:           'url': 'https://' ~ _fqdn,
    33:           'probe_url': _probe_url,
    34:         }]
    35:       }}
    36:   vars:
    37:     _host: "{{ item.hostname | default(item.name, true) }}"
    38:     _fqdn: >-
    39:       {{ dashboard_catalog_base_domain if (item.apex | default(false))
    40:          else (_host ~ '.' ~ dashboard_catalog_base_domain) }}
    41:     # Status widgets issue an UNAUTHENTICATED HEAD. Pointed at the public URL
    42:     # they are answered by Authelia's HTML login page and every service reads as
    43:     # down, so a probe addresses the guest directly. This is the same reason the
    44:     # homarr role talks to homarr_api_base rather than its own vhost. A probe is
    45:     # never a link: nothing a person clicks goes here.
    46:     #
    47:     # Pool-backed rows carry `backends` instead of a single `ip`; the first
    48:     # backend is a fine liveness target, and rows with neither get no probe
    49:     # rather than a fabricated one.
    50:     _probe_host: "{{ item.ip | default((item.backends | default([]))[0] | default(''), true) }}"
    51:     _probe_scheme: "{{ item.scheme | default('http') }}"
    52:     _probe_port: "{{ item.port | default('') | string }}"
    53:     _probe_url: >-
    54:       {{ (_probe_host | length > 0)
    55:          | ternary(_probe_scheme ~ '://' ~ _probe_host ~ ':' ~ _probe_port, '') }}
    56:   loop: "{{ dashboard_catalog_ingress }}"
    57:   loop_control:
    58:     label: "{{ item.name }} [{{ item.group | default('other', true) }}]"
    59: 
    60: - name: Order the catalog by group, then name
    61:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    62:     dashboard_catalog_services: >-
    63:       {{ dashboard_catalog_services
    64:          | sort(attribute='name')
    65:          | sort(attribute='group') }}
    66: 
    67: # EVERY default of this role that a board role consumes must be re-exported as
    68: # a fact. A role default is in scope only inside its own role, so a board role
    69: # rendering a template that names one fails with "... is undefined".
    70: #
    71: # Export the whole class, not the one variable a failure happens to name: the
    72: # first fix here covered only group_order, and the next converge failed on
    73: # base_domain for exactly the same reason. These three are what
    74: # `grep -rhoE 'dashboard_catalog_[a-z_]+' roles/{homepage,glance,homarr}`
    75: # returns; services is already a fact from the set_fact above.
    76: - name: Export the catalog's own settings as facts for the board roles
    77:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    78:     dashboard_catalog_group_order: "{{ dashboard_catalog_group_order }}"
    79:     dashboard_catalog_base_domain: "{{ dashboard_catalog_base_domain }}"
    80: 
    81: - name: Report the catalog the boards will render
    82:   ansible.builtin.debug:
    83:     msg: >-
    84:       {{ dashboard_catalog_services | length }} services across
    85:       {{ dashboard_catalog_services | map(attribute='group') | unique | sort | list }}

name: roles/postgres/tasks/main/cluster_config.yml
review_question: Would an Ansible expert judge this playbook or task file as needing abstraction because it contains too many direct leaf tasks?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # =============================================================================
     3: # Phase 3: Cluster configuration (idempotent GUCs)
     4: # postgresql_set only writes when the value differs, so the idempotence run is
     5: # clean. listen_addresses/port need a restart; password_encryption reloads.
     6: # =============================================================================
     7: - name: Configure cluster GUCs
     8:   become: true
     9:   become_user: postgres
    10:   vars:
    11:     ansible_ssh_pipelining: true
    12:   block:
    13:     - name: Set listen_addresses
    14:       community.postgresql.postgresql_set:
    15:         name: listen_addresses
    16:         value: "{{ postgres_listen_addresses }}"
    17:       notify: Restart postgresql
    18: 
    19:     - name: Set port
    20:       community.postgresql.postgresql_set:
    21:         name: port
    22:         value: "{{ postgres_port }}"
    23:       notify: Restart postgresql
    24: 
    25:     - name: Enforce scram-sha-256 password encryption
    26:       community.postgresql.postgresql_set:
    27:         name: password_encryption
    28:         value: "{{ postgres_password_encryption }}"
    29:       notify: Reload postgresql
    30: 
    31: # Apply a pending restart NOW so the remote listener + scram are live before we
    32: # create roles and run the health check (handlers otherwise flush at play end).
    33: - name: Apply pending PostgreSQL restart/reload
    34:   ansible.builtin.meta: flush_handlers
    35: 
    36: # A cluster that comes up listening only on loopback is invisible to every
    37: # other guest, and nothing downstream notices until an app tier starts timing
    38: # out — which is how this surfaced once already: apps could not reach the
    39: # shared database, and the failure looked like connection-pool exhaustion
    40: # rather than a missing listener. The GUC being set is not proof the listener
    41: # is live; only a bind off loopback is. Assert it here, right after the
    42: # restart, so a divergence fails this converge instead of a later outage.
    43: # Read the bound sockets on the guest itself. Deliberately NOT a connect from
    44: # the control node: a workstation controller is often firewalled off the guest
    45: # VLAN, so that would fail for hosts that are perfectly healthy. What the guest
    46: # is bound to is the fact that matters, and it is knowable locally.
    47: - name: List the bound PostgreSQL sockets
    48:   ansible.builtin.command:
    49:     argv: [ss, -H, -ltn, "sport = :{{ postgres_port }}"]
    50:   register: postgres_bound_sockets
    51:   changed_when: false
    52:   failed_when: false
    53: 
    54: # ss prints the local address in column 4 (host:port). Anything bound to
    55: # 0.0.0.0, [::] or a real interface address is reachable off-box; only
    56: # 127.0.0.1/[::1] is not.
    57: #
    58: # Why a restart rather than going straight to the assert: postgresql_set is
    59: # idempotent against the STORED setting, not the runtime bind. ALTER SYSTEM
    60: # writes $PGDATA/postgresql.auto.conf, so once the correct value is stored
    61: # every later converge is a no-op — changed=false, the restart handler never
    62: # fires, and flush_handlers has nothing to flush. If the server started before
    63: # the container NIC was up it binds loopback, fails to bind the real address,
    64: # and does NOT exit (a partial bind failure is a warning; only a total failure
    65: # is fatal). The config is right and the process is wrong, which is a state
    66: # Ansible can repair on its own. Restart, re-read, and let the assert below
    67: # fail only if the restart did not fix it.
    68: - name: Restart the cluster when it is bound loopback-only
    69:   vars:
    70:     postgres_local_addrs: >-
    71:       {{ postgres_bound_sockets.stdout_lines | default([])
    72:          | map('split') | map(attribute=3)
    73:          | map('regex_replace', ':[0-9]+$', '') | list }}
    74:   ansible.builtin.systemd:
    75:     name: "postgresql@{{ postgres_cluster_version }}-{{ postgres_cluster_name }}"
    76:     state: restarted
    77:   when:
    78:     - postgres_listen_addresses not in ['localhost', '127.0.0.1', '::1']
    79:     - postgres_local_addrs | reject('in', ['127.0.0.1', '[::1]']) | list | length == 0
    80: 
    81: - name: Re-read the bound PostgreSQL sockets after the repair restart
    82:   ansible.builtin.command:
    83:     argv: [ss, -H, -ltn, "sport = :{{ postgres_port }}"]
    84:   register: postgres_bound_sockets
    85:   changed_when: false
    86:   failed_when: false
    87: 
    88: - name: Fail when the cluster is still listening on loopback only
    89:   vars:
    90:     postgres_local_addrs: >-
    91:       {{ postgres_bound_sockets.stdout_lines | default([])
    92:          | map('split') | map(attribute=3)
    93:          | map('regex_replace', ':[0-9]+$', '') | list }}
    94:   ansible.builtin.assert:
    95:     that:
    96:       - postgres_local_addrs | reject('in', ['127.0.0.1', '[::1]']) | list | length > 0
    97:     fail_msg: >-
    98:       PostgreSQL on {{ inventory_hostname }} is bound only to
    99:       {{ postgres_local_addrs | default([], true) }} even after a restart, so
   100:       no other guest can reach it on port {{ postgres_port }}. Expected a
   101:       listener matching
   102:       postgres_listen_addresses={{ postgres_listen_addresses }}. Since the
   103:       restart did not fix it, the stored setting itself is wrong or the address
   104:       does not exist on this guest — check
   105:       `SHOW listen_addresses` and the interface addresses, not just the config.
   106:     success_msg: >-
   107:       PostgreSQL is reachable off loopback (bound: {{ postgres_local_addrs }}).
   108:   when: postgres_listen_addresses not in ['localhost', '127.0.0.1', '::1']

    17: - name: Post deployment descriptors for remote modules

    19:   when: folio_install_type == "single_server" and item.url is defined

    22: - name: Build tenant parameter list

    35:   with_items: "{{ tenant_parameters }}"
    36: 
    37: - name: Create dict for install object

name: roles/edge-module/tasks/main.yml

source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Setup
     3: - name: Create configuration directory
     4:   become: yes
     5:   file:
     6:     path: "{{ edge_conf_dir }}"
     7:     state: directory
     8: 
     9: - name: Copy authentication store
    10:   become: yes
    11:   template:
    12:     src: ephemeral.properties
    13:     dest: "{{ edge_conf_dir }}/{{ edge_module }}-ephemeral.properties"
    14:     mode: 0644
    15: 
    16: # Set up institutional user
    17: - name: Login as {{ admin_user.username }}
    18:   uri:
    19:     url: "{{ okapi_url }}/authn/login"
    20:     method: POST
    21:     body_format: json
    22:     headers:
    23:       X-Okapi-Tenant: "{{ tenant }}"
    24:       Accept: application/json
    25:     body: "{ 'username' : '{{ admin_user.username }}', 'password' : '{{ admin_user.password }}' }"
    26:     status_code: 201
    27:   register: tenant_admin_login
    28:   when: auth_required
    29: 
    30: - name: Check institutional user
    31:   uri:
    32:     url: "{{ okapi_url }}/users?query=username%3d%3d{{ inst_user.username }}"
    33:     headers:
    34:       X-Okapi-Tenant: "{{ tenant }}"
    35:       X-Okapi-Token: "{{ tenant_admin_login.x_okapi_token|default('token') }}"
    36:       Accept: application/json
    37:     status_code: 200
    38:   register: check_inst_user
    39: 
    40: - name: Create institutional user
    41:   uri:
    42:     url: "{{ okapi_url }}/users"
    43:     method: POST
    44:     body_format: json
    45:     headers:
    46:       X-Okapi-Tenant: "{{ tenant }}"
    47:       X-Okapi-Token: "{{ tenant_admin_login.x_okapi_token|default('token') }}"
    48:       Accept: application/json
    49:     body: |
    50:       {
    51:         "id": "{{ 9999999999999999999998 | random | to_uuid }}",
    52:         "username": "{{ inst_user.username }}",
    53:         "active": true{% if inst_user.personal|default(false) %},
    54:         "personal": {{ inst_user.personal|to_json(ensure_ascii=False) }}{% endif %}
    55:       }
    56:     status_code: 201
    57:   when: check_inst_user.json.totalRecords == 0
    58:   register: create_inst_user
    59:   changed_when: create_inst_user.status == 201
    60: 
    61: - name: Get institutional user UUID variable
    62:   set_fact:
    63:     inst_user_uuid: "{% if check_inst_user.json.users.0|default(false) %}{{ check_inst_user.json.users.0.id }}{% else %}{{ create_inst_user.json.id }}{% endif %}"
    64: 
    65: - name: Check institutional user login record
    66:   uri:
    67:     url: "{{ okapi_url }}/authn/credentials-existence?userId={{ inst_user_uuid }}"
    68:     headers:
    69:       X-Okapi-Tenant: "{{ tenant }}"
    70:       X-Okapi-Token: "{{ tenant_admin_login.x_okapi_token|default('token') }}"
    71:       Accept: application/json
    72:     status_code: 200
    73:   register: check_inst_login
    74: 
    75: - name: Create institutional user login record
    76:   uri:
    77:     url: "{{ okapi_url }}/authn/credentials"
    78:     method: POST
    79:     body_format: json
    80:     headers:
    81:       X-Okapi-Tenant: "{{ tenant }}"
    82:       X-Okapi-Token: "{{ tenant_admin_login.x_okapi_token|default('token') }}"
    83:       Accept: application/json
    84:     body: |
    85:       {
    86:         "userId": "{{ inst_user_uuid }}",
    87:         "password": "{{ inst_user.password }}"
    88:       }
    89:     status_code: 201
    90:   when: check_inst_login.json.credentialsExist == false
    91:   register: create_inst_login
    92:   changed_when: create_inst_login.status == 201
    93: 
    94: - name: Check institutional user permissions record
    95:   uri:
    96:     url: "{{ okapi_url }}/perms/users?query=userId%3d%3d{{ inst_user_uuid }}"
    97:     headers:
    98:       X-Okapi-Tenant: "{{ tenant }}"
    99:       X-Okapi-Token: "{{ tenant_admin_login.x_okapi_token|default('token') }}"
   100:       Accept: application/json
   101:     status_code: 200
   102:   register: check_inst_perms
   103: 
   104: - name: Create institutional user permissions record
   105:   uri:
   106:     url: "{{ okapi_url }}/perms/users"
   107:     method: POST
   108:     body_format: json
   109:     headers:
   110:       X-Okapi-Tenant: "{{ tenant }}"
   111:       X-Okapi-Token: "{{ tenant_admin_login.x_okapi_token|default('token') }}"
   112:       Accept: application/json
   113:     body: |
   114:       {
   115:         "userId": "{{ inst_user_uuid }}"
   116:       }
   117:     status_code: 201
   118:   when: check_inst_perms.json.totalRecords == 0
   119:   register: create_inst_perms
   120:   changed_when: create_inst_perms.status == 201
   121: 
   122: - name: Get institutional user perms UUID
   123:   set_fact:
   124:     inst_perms_uuid: "{% if check_inst_perms.json.permissionUsers.0|default(false) %}{{ check_inst_perms.json.permissionUsers.0.id }}{% else %}{{ create_inst_perms.json.id }}{% endif %}"
   125: 
   126: - name: Get assigned permissions for institutional user
   127:   set_fact:
   128:     inst_user_assigned_perms: "{% if check_inst_perms.json.permissionUsers.0|default(false) %}{{ check_inst_perms.json.permissionUsers.0.permissions }}{% else %}{{ [ ] }}{% endif %}"
   129: 
   130: - name: Assign permissions to {{ inst_user.username }}
   131:   uri:
   132:     url: "{{ okapi_url }}/perms/users/{{ inst_perms_uuid }}/permissions"
   133:     method: POST
   134:     headers:
   135:       X-Okapi-Tenant: "{{ tenant }}"
   136:       X-Okapi-Token: "{{ tenant_admin_login.x_okapi_token|default('token') }}"
   137:       Accept: application/json
   138:     body: '{ "permissionName" : "{{ item }}" }'
   139:     body_format: json
   140:     status_code: 200
   141:   when: "[ item ]|difference(inst_user_assigned_perms)"
   142:   register: inst_user_assign_perms
   143:   with_items: "{{ inst_user_perms }}"
   144:   changed_when: inst_user_assign_perms.status == 200
   145: 
   146: # Get module version
   147: - name: Get tenant modules
   148:   uri:
   149:     url: "{{ okapi_url }}/_/proxy/tenants/{{ tenant }}/modules"
   150:     headers:
   151:       X-Okapi-Tenant: "supertenant"
   152:       X-Okapi-Token: "{{ supertenant_token | default('') }}"
   153:       Accept: application/json
   154:   register: tenant_modules
   155: 
   156: - name: Reset tenant_module_id
   157:   set_fact:
   158:     tenant_module_id: ''
   159: 
   160: - name: Get ID of module for tenant
   161:   set_fact:
   162:     tenant_module_id: "{{ item.id }}"
   163:   when: item.id is search(edge_module)
   164:   with_items: "{{ tenant_modules.json }}"
   165: 
   166: - fail: msg="{{ edge_module }} not initialized for {{ tenant }}"
   167:   when: tenant_module_id == ''
   168: 
   169: - name: Get version
   170:   set_fact:
   171:     edge_module_version: "{{ tenant_module_id|regex_search('([0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+.*$)') }}"
   172: 
   173: # Launch container
   174: - name: Launch container for edge module
   175:   become: yes
   176:   docker_container:
   177:     name: "{{ edge_module }}-{{ edge_module_version }}"
   178:     image: "{{ edge_docker_repo }}/{{ edge_module }}:{{ edge_module_version }}"
   179:     env: "{{ edge_module_docker_env }}"
   180:     command:
   181:       - "{{ edge_module_cmd }}"
   182:     keep_volumes: no
   183:     published_ports: "{{ edge_module_publish_port }}:{{ edge_module_expose_port }}"
   184:     restart_policy: always
   185:     state: started
   186:     volumes: "{{ edge_conf_dir }}:/mnt"
   187:     memory: "{{ edge_module_memory }}"
   188: 
   189: # Set up nginx proxy
   190: - name: Copy edge_module_path
   191:   set_fact:
   192:     edge_module_path_working: "{{ edge_module_path }}"
   193:   when: edge_nginx_proxy|default(true)
   194: 
   195: - name: Turn edge_module_path into a list
   196:   set_fact:
   197:     edge_module_path_working: "{{ [ edge_module_path_working ] }}"
   198:   when: edge_nginx_proxy|default(true) and edge_module_path_working|type_debug != "list"
   199: 
   200: - name: Configure nginx
   201:   become: yes
   202:   blockinfile:
   203:     dest: /etc/nginx/sites-available/edge
   204:     marker: "# {mark} {{ edge_module }}-{{ path_idx }} ANSIBLE MANAGED BLOCK"
   205:     insertbefore: "^}\\s*$"
   206:     block: |
   207:       location {{ item }} {
   208:         proxy_pass http://localhost:{{ edge_module_publish_port }};
   209:       {% if edge_http_version|default(false) %}
   210:         proxy_http_version {{ edge_http_version }};
   211:       {% endif %}
   212:       }
   213:   notify: Restart nginx
   214:   loop: "{{ edge_module_path_working }}"
   215:   loop_control:
   216:     index_var: path_idx
   217:   when: edge_nginx_proxy|default(true)
   218: 
   219: - meta: flush_handlers

    10:     - "{{ role_path }}/vars/{{ ansible_facts['distribution'] }}-{{ ansible_facts['distribution_major_version'] }}.yml"
    11:     - "{{ role_path }}/vars/{{ ansible_facts['distribution'] }}.yml"
    12:     # os_family is used as a fallback for distros which are not currently
    13:     # supported, but are based on a supported distro family. For example,
    14:     # Oracle, Rocky, Alma and Alibaba linux, which are all "RedHat" based.
    15:     - "vars/{{ ansible_facts['os_family'] }}-{{ ansible_facts['distribution_version'] }}.yml"
    16:     - "vars/{{ ansible_facts['os_family'] }}-{{ ansible_facts['distribution_major_version'] }}.yml"
    17:     - "vars/{{ ansible_facts['os_family'] }}.yml"
    18:     # If neither distro nor family is supported, try a default configuration.
    19:     - "{{ role_path }}/vars/default.yml"
    20: 
    21: ### GET SERVICES FROM BACKUP
    22: 
    23: - name: Stat backup on server
    24:   ansible.builtin.stat:
    25:     path: "{{ ipabackup_dir }}/{{ ipabackup_item }}"
    26:   register: result_backup_stat
    27: 
    28: - name: Fail on missing backup directory

    30:     msg: "Unable to find backup {{ ipabackup_item }}"
    31:   when: result_backup_stat.stat.isdir is not defined
    32: 
    33: - name: Stat header file in backup "{{ ipabackup_item }}"
    34:   ansible.builtin.stat:
    35:     path: "{{ ipabackup_dir }}/{{ ipabackup_item }}/header"
    36:   register: result_backup_header_stat
    37: 
    38: - name: Fail on missing header file in backup
    39:   ansible.builtin.fail:
    40:     msg: "Unable to find backup {{ ipabackup_item }} header file"
    41:   when: result_backup_header_stat.stat.isreg is not defined
    42: 
    43: - name: Get services from backup
    44:   ansible.builtin.shell: >
    45:     grep "^services = " "{{ ipabackup_dir }}/{{ ipabackup_item }}/header" | cut -d"=" -f2 | tr -d '[:space:]'
    46:   register: result_services_grep
    47: 
    48: - name: Set ipabackup_services
    49:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    50:     ipabackup_services: "{{ result_services_grep.stdout.split(',') }}"

    60:   - name: Ensure that IPA server packages are installed

    62:       name: "{{ ipaserver_packages }}"
    63:       state: present
    64: 
    65:   - name: Ensure that IPA server packages for dns are installed

    67:       name: "{{ ipaserver_packages_dns }}"
    68:       state: present
    69:     when: ipabackup_service_dns in ipabackup_services
    70: 
    71:   - name: Ensure that IPA server packages for adtrust are installed

    74:       state: present
    75:     when: ipabackup_service_adtrust in ipabackup_services

    77:   - name: Ensure that firewalld packages are installed

    79:       name: "{{ ipaserver_packages_firewalld }}"
    80:       state: present
    81:     when: ipabackup_setup_firewalld | bool
    82: 
    83: ### START FIREWALLD

    85: - name: Firewall configuration

    91:       enabled: yes
    92:       state: started
    93: 
    94:   - name: Firewalld - Verify zones
    95:     when: ipabackup_firewalld_zone is defined
    96:     block:
    97:     - name: Firewalld - Verify runtime zone from ipabackup_firewalld_zone
    98:       ansible.builtin.shell: >
    99:         firewall-cmd
   100:         --info-zone="{{ ipabackup_firewalld_zone }}"
   101:         >/dev/null
   102: 
   103:     - name: Firewalld - Verify permanent zone from ipabackup_firewalld_zone
   104:       ansible.builtin.shell: >
   105:         firewall-cmd
   106:         --permanent
   107:         --info-zone="{{ ipabackup_firewalld_zone }}"
   108:         >/dev/null
   109: 
   110: ### RESTORE
   111: 
   112: - name: Restore backup
   113:   no_log: True
   114:   ansible.builtin.shell: >
   115:     ipa-restore
   116:     {{ ipabackup_item }}
   117:     --unattended
   118:     {{ "--password=" + ipabackup_password if ipabackup_password is defined else "" }}
   119:     {{ "--data" if ipabackup_data | bool else "" }}
   120:     {{ "--online" if ipabackup_online | bool else "" }}
   121:     {{ "--instance=" + ipabackup_instance if ipabackup_instance is defined else "" }}
   122:     {{ "--backend=" + ipabackup_backend if ipabackup_backend is defined else "" }}
   123:     {{ "--no-logs" if ipabackup_no_logs | bool else "" }}
   124:     {{ "--log-file=" + ipabackup_log_file if ipabackup_log_file is defined else "" }}
   125:   register: result_iparestore
   126:   ignore_errors: yes
   127: 
   128: - name: Report error for restore operation
   129:   ansible.builtin.debug:
   130:     msg: "{{ result_iparestore.stderr }}"
   131:   when: result_iparestore is failed
   132:   failed_when: yes
   133: 
   134: ### CONFIGURE FIREWALLD
   135: 
   136: - name: Configure firewalld
   137:   ansible.builtin.command: >
   138:     firewall-cmd
   139:     --permanent
   140:     {{ "--zone=" + ipabackup_firewalld_zone if ipabackup_firewalld_zone is defined else "" }}
   141:     --add-service=freeipa-ldap
   142:     --add-service=freeipa-ldaps
   143:     {{ "--add-service=freeipa-trust" if ipabackup_service_adtrust in ipabackup_services else "" }}
   144:     {{ "--add-service=dns" if ipabackup_service_dns in ipabackup_services else "" }}
   145:     {{ "--add-service=ntp" if ipabackup_service_ntp in ipabackup_services else "" }}
   146:   when: ipabackup_setup_firewalld | bool
   147: 
   148: - name: Configure firewalld runtime
   149:   ansible.builtin.command: >
   150:     firewall-cmd
   151:     {{ "--zone=" + ipabackup_firewalld_zone if ipabackup_firewalld_zone is defined else "" }}
   152:     --add-service=freeipa-ldap

source_context:
1: ---
     2: #
     3: # These tasks build /etc contents that will be copied to the target filesystem
     4: # to override the default configs of the respective packages and system parts.
     5: #
     6: # We copy Jinja2 templates (from ../templates) and static files (from ../files).
     7: # Files are simply copied, templates are rendered and then written to /etc.
     8: #
     9: # Symlinks can be used for individual files, but not for directories.
    10: # If symlinks were used for directories too, we couldn't tell whether the
    11: # symlink target is a file or a directory - Ansible doesn't seem to let us.
    12: #
    13: # Possible future additions:
    14: # - preserve permissions
    15: # - ability to remove files, not just to add or change/override them
    16: # - collapse files/ into templates/ and treat everything as a template
    17: #
    18: 
    19: - name: Create /etc directories for template output
    20:   tags: always
    21:   file:
    22:     path: "{{ configs_dir }}/etc/{{ item.path }}"
    23:     state: directory
    24:     mode: "755"
    25:   loop: "{{ lookup('community.general.filetree', role_path + '/templates/' + role) }}"
    26:   when: item.state == 'directory'
    27:   loop_control:
    28:     label: "{{ item.path }}"
    29: 
    30: - name: Create /etc directories for static files
    31:   tags: always
    32:   file:
    33:     path: "{{ configs_dir }}/etc/{{ item.path }}"
    34:     state: directory
    35:     mode: "755"
    36:   loop: "{{ lookup('community.general.filetree', role_path + '/files/' + role) }}"
    37:   when: item.state == 'directory'
    38:   loop_control:
    39:     label: "{{ item.path }}"
    40: 
    41: - name: Render /etc templates
    42:   tags: always
    43:   template:
    44:     src: "{{ item.root }}/{{ item.path }}"
    45:     dest: "{{ configs_dir }}/etc/{{ item.path | regex_replace('.j2$', '') }}"
    46:     mode: "644"
    47:   loop: "{{ lookup('community.general.filetree', role_path + '/templates/' + role) }}"
    48:   when: item.path is regex('\.j2$')
    49:   loop_control:
    50:     label: "{{ item.path }}"
    51: 
    52: - name: Copy /etc static files
    53:   tags: always
    54:   copy:
    55:     src: "{{ item.root }}/{{ item.path }}"
    56:     dest: "{{ configs_dir }}/etc/{{ item.path }}"
    57:     mode: "preserve"
    58:   loop: "{{ lookup('community.general.filetree', role_path + '/files/' + role) }}"
    59:   when: (not item.path is regex('\.j2$')) and (item.state == 'file' or item.state == 'link')
    60:   loop_control:
    61:     label: "{{ item.path }}"
    62: 
    63: - name: Create rootfs directories for static files
    64:   tags: always
    65:   file:
    66:     path: "{{ configs_dir }}/{{ item.path }}"
    67:     state: directory
    68:     mode: "755"
    69:   loop: "{{ lookup('community.general.filetree', role_path + '/rootfs/' + role, errors='ignore') }}"
    70:   when: item.state == 'directory'
    71:   loop_control:
    72:     label: "{{ item.path }}"
    73: 
    74: - name: Copy rootfs static files
    75:   tags: always
    76:   copy:
    77:     src: "{{ item.root }}/{{ item.path }}"
    78:     dest: "{{ configs_dir }}/{{ item.path }}"
    79:     mode: "preserve"
    80:   loop: "{{ lookup('community.general.filetree', role_path + '/rootfs/' + role, errors='ignore') }}"
    81:   when: (not item.path is regex('\.j2$')) and (item.state == 'file' or item.state == 'link')
    82:   loop_control:
    83:     label: "{{ item.path }}"

    12: # Runs on localhost ON PURPOSE (same rationale as
    13: # bootstrap-connect-credential.yml): it never loads group_vars/aap, and it
    14: # talks to the gateway tokens API with per-user basic auth because AAP 2.6
    15: # removed controller-local token minting; gateway tokens are shown once at
    16: # creation, hence the immediate 1Password upsert.
    17: #
    18: # Re-running mints fresh tokens and replaces the 1P items (old tokens keep
    19: # working in AAP until deleted in the UI — prune old "mcp-client" tokens
    20: # there when rotating).
    21: #
    22: # Prereqs: OP_CONNECT_HOST + OP_CONNECT_TOKEN in the runner env (devcontainer
    23: # default), Connect token able to read/write lab_aap.
    24: #
    25: # Run:
    26: #   ANSIBLE_NAVIGATOR_CONFIG=playbooks/aap/ansible-navigator.yml \
    27: #     ansible-navigator run playbooks/aap/mint-mcp-tokens.yml --mode stdout
    28: - name: Mint AAP MCP gateway tokens and publish to 1Password
    29:   hosts: localhost
    30:   connection: local
    31:   gather_facts: false
    32:   vars:
    33:     # the 1P host field carries the scheme — strip it so the url below works
    34:     aap_hostname: "{{ lookup('community.general.onepassword', 'aap', field='host', vault='lab_aap') | regex_replace('^https?://', '') }}"
    35:     op_connect_host: "{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.env', 'OP_CONNECT_HOST') }}"
    36:     op_connect_token: "{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.env', 'OP_CONNECT_TOKEN') }}"
    37:     mcp_token_users:
    38:       - persona: igou
    39:         aap_username: "{{ lookup('community.general.onepassword', 'aap', field='username', vault='lab_aap') }}"
    40:         aap_password: "{{ lookup('community.general.onepassword', 'aap', field='password', vault='lab_aap') }}"
    41:         op_item: aap-mcp-token-igou
    42:       - persona: dev1
    43:         aap_username: "{{ lookup('community.general.onepassword', 'aap-dev1', field='username', vault='lab_aap') }}"
    44:         aap_password: "{{ lookup('community.general.onepassword', 'aap-dev1', field='password', vault='lab_aap') }}"
    45:         op_item: aap-mcp-token-dev1
    46:   tasks:
    47:     - name: Mint a gateway OAuth token per persona
    48:       ansible.builtin.uri:
    49:         url: "https://{{ aap_hostname }}/api/gateway/v1/tokens/"
    50:         method: POST
    51:         url_username: "{{ item.aap_username }}"
    52:         url_password: "{{ item.aap_password }}"
    53:         force_basic_auth: true
    54:         body_format: json
    55:         body:
    56:           description: "mcp-client ({{ item.persona }})"
    57:           # write includes read; launching templates through MCP needs it.
    58:           # dev1's lock-down comes from RBAC (sandbox org only), not scope.
    59:           scope: write
    60:         status_code: [201]
    61:       loop: "{{ mcp_token_users }}"
    62:       loop_control:
    63:         label: "{{ item.persona }}"
    64:       register: minted
    65:       no_log: true
    66: 
    67:     - name: Resolve lab_aap vault id
    68:       ansible.builtin.uri:
    69:         url: "{{ op_connect_host }}/v1/vaults?filter={{ 'name eq \"lab_aap\"' | urlencode }}"
    70:         headers:
    71:           Authorization: "Bearer {{ op_connect_token }}"
    72:       register: op_vault
    73:       no_log: true
    74: 
    75:     - name: Look up existing token items
    76:       ansible.builtin.uri:
    77:         url: "{{ op_connect_host }}/v1/vaults/{{ op_vault.json[0].id }}/items?filter={{ ('title eq \"' ~ item.item.op_item ~ '\"') | urlencode }}"
    78:         headers:
    79:           Authorization: "Bearer {{ op_connect_token }}"
    80:       loop: "{{ minted.results }}"
    81:       loop_control:
    82:         label: "{{ item.item.op_item }}"
    83:       register: op_existing
    84:       no_log: true
    85: 
    86:     - name: Create or replace the 1Password token items
    87:       ansible.builtin.uri:
    88:         url: >-
    89:           {{ op_connect_host }}/v1/vaults/{{ op_vault.json[0].id }}/items{{
    90:             '/' + item.1.json[0].id if item.1.json | length > 0 else '' }}
    91:         method: "{{ 'PUT' if item.1.json | length > 0 else 'POST' }}"
    92:         headers:
    93:           Authorization: "Bearer {{ op_connect_token }}"
    94:         body_format: json
    95:         body:
    96:           id: "{{ item.1.json[0].id if item.1.json | length > 0 else omit }}"
    97:           title: "{{ item.0.item.op_item }}"
    98:           category: API_CREDENTIAL
    99:           vault:
   100:             id: "{{ op_vault.json[0].id }}"
   101:           fields:
   102:             - id: token
   103:               label: token
   104:               type: CONCEALED
   105:               value: "{{ item.0.json.token }}"
   106:         status_code: [200, 201]
   107:       loop: "{{ minted.results | zip(op_existing.results) | list }}"
   108:       loop_control:
   109:         label: "{{ item.0.item.op_item }}"
   110:       no_log: true
   111: 
   112:     - name: Report published items
   113:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   114:         msg: "Published {{ mcp_token_users | map(attribute='op_item') | join(', ') }} to lab_aap"

name: playbooks/windows/provision_test_machine.yaml
review_question: Would an Ansible expert judge this playbook or task file as needing abstraction because it contains too many direct leaf tasks?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Provision a Windows machine as a self-contained application test bed:
     3: # create a dedicated test user, install a configurable set of applications,
     4: # and (optionally) open Remote Desktop so an interactive agent can log in
     5: # and drive the GUI.
     6: #
     7: # Written for — but not limited to — Windows VMs running on OpenShift
     8: # Virtualization, where an automation agent later signs in as the test user
     9: # to exercise the installed applications. See README.md for how a fresh VM
    10: # gets its first WinRM/SSH listener (sysprep answer file or cloudbase-init);
    11: # this play takes over from the moment Ansible can connect.
    12: #
    13: # This play composes the building blocks shown in manage_local_users.yaml
    14: # and install_applications.yaml — read those two for the full option set.
    15: #
    16: # Targeting: pass ansible_limit=<host-or-group>. Defaults to the 'windows'
    17: # inventory group.
    18: #
    19: # Variables:
    20: #   windows_test_user           - test account to create (default 'apptester')
    21: #   windows_test_user_password  - REQUIRED. Pass via extra_vars, e.g.
    22: #                                 -e windows_test_user_password="{{ lookup('community.general.onepassword',
    23: #                                    'windows-apptester', field='password', vault='lab_agents') }}"
    24: #                                 Must satisfy the default Windows password
    25: #                                 complexity policy (length + character
    26: #                                 classes) or win_user rejects it and the
    27: #                                 play fails.
    28: #   windows_test_user_groups    - local groups for the account
    29: #                                 (default: Users + Remote Desktop Users)
    30: #   windows_test_apps           - Chocolatey packages to install; a list of
    31: #                                 dicts with name / version (optional) /
    32: #                                 state (optional, default present)
    33: #   windows_test_msi_packages   - extra MSI/EXE installers not available in
    34: #                                 Chocolatey; list of dicts with path (local
    35: #                                 path or URL), product_id, arguments,
    36: #                                 creates_path (see win_package docs).
    37: #                                 Default: none.
    38: #   windows_test_enable_rdp     - enable Remote Desktop + firewall rule so
    39: #                                 GUI agents can connect (default true)
    40: #
    41: # Run:
    42: #   ansible-navigator run playbooks/windows/provision_test_machine.yaml \
    43: #     -i igou-inventory/inventory.yaml -e ansible_limit=<vm-host> \
    44: #     -e windows_test_user_password=<secret>
    45: - name: Provision a Windows application test machine
    46:   hosts: "{{ ansible_limit | default('windows') }}"
    47:   gather_facts: false
    48: 
    49:   vars:
    50:     windows_test_user: apptester
    51:     windows_test_user_groups:
    52:       - Users
    53:       - Remote Desktop Users
    54:     windows_test_apps:
    55:       - name: git
    56:       - name: 7zip
    57:       - name: notepadplusplus
    58:     windows_test_msi_packages: []
    59:     windows_test_enable_rdp: true
    60: 
    61:   tasks:
    62:     # Fail fast with a clear message instead of a mid-play "undefined
    63:     # variable" error — passwords must come from extra_vars or a vault,
    64:     # never from a file checked into git.
    65:     - name: Make sure a password was provided for the test user
    66:       ansible.builtin.assert:
    67:         that:
    68:           - windows_test_user_password is defined
    69:           - windows_test_user_password | default('') | length > 0
    70:         fail_msg: >-
    71:           Set windows_test_user_password via extra_vars (ideally from a
    72:           1Password lookup) — see the header of this playbook.
    73: 
    74:     # --- Test user -------------------------------------------------------
    75:     # no_log hides the module arguments (which include the password) from
    76:     # logs and console output. update_password: on_create keeps the play
    77:     # idempotent — reruns won't reset a password the user already rotated.
    78:     - name: Create the application test user
    79:       ansible.windows.win_user:
    80:         name: "{{ windows_test_user }}"
    81:         password: "{{ windows_test_user_password }}"
    82:         update_password: on_create
    83:         password_never_expires: true
    84:         description: Application test account managed by Ansible
    85:         groups: "{{ windows_test_user_groups }}"
    86:         groups_action: add
    87:         state: present
    88:       no_log: true
    89: 
    90:     # --- Applications ----------------------------------------------------
    91:     # Chocolatey's bootstrap runs a downloaded .ps1, which the default
    92:     # execution policy on Windows CLIENT SKUs (Restricted) blocks — the
    93:     # bootstrap dies with "running scripts is disabled on this system".
    94:     # Ensure at least RemoteSigned (the Windows Server default, which
    95:     # permits locally-created unsigned scripts) at LocalMachine scope so
    96:     # the bootstrap can run. Idempotent: only writes when the policy is
    97:     # more restrictive than RemoteSigned/Unrestricted/Bypass. Same fix as
    98:     # install_applications.yaml.
    99:     - name: Ensure the execution policy permits the Chocolatey bootstrap
   100:       ansible.windows.win_shell: |
   101:         $ok = @('RemoteSigned', 'Unrestricted', 'Bypass')
   102:         if ((Get-ExecutionPolicy -Scope LocalMachine) -notin $ok) {
   103:           Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope LocalMachine -Force
   104:           'changed'
   105:         } else {
   106:           'ok'
   107:         }
   108:       register: windows_test_execpolicy
   109:       changed_when: "'changed' in windows_test_execpolicy.stdout"
   110: 
   111:     # The first win_chocolatey run bootstraps Chocolatey itself from the
   112:     # internet, so the VM needs outbound HTTPS (or set an internal source —
   113:     # see install_applications.yaml).
   114:     - name: Install test applications with Chocolatey
   115:       chocolatey.chocolatey.win_chocolatey:
   116:         name: "{{ item.name }}"
   117:         version: "{{ item.version | default(omit) }}"
   118:         state: "{{ item.state | default('present') }}"
   119:       loop: "{{ windows_test_apps }}"
   120:       loop_control:
   121:         label: "{{ item.name }}"
   122: 
   123:     # win_package handles anything Chocolatey can't: vendor MSIs, EXE
   124:     # installers from a share or URL. product_id is what makes reruns
   125:     # idempotent — without it (or creates_path) the installer runs again
   126:     # every time.
   127:     - name: Install extra MSI/EXE packages
   128:       ansible.windows.win_package:
   129:         path: "{{ item.path }}"
   130:         product_id: "{{ item.product_id | default(omit) }}"
   131:         arguments: "{{ item.arguments | default(omit) }}"
   132:         creates_path: "{{ item.creates_path | default(omit) }}"
   133:         state: present
   134:       loop: "{{ windows_test_msi_packages }}"
   135:       loop_control:
   136:         label: "{{ item.path }}"
   137: 
   138:     # --- Remote Desktop (optional) ----------------------------------------
   139:     # Three pieces make RDP reachable: the registry switch that allows
   140:     # connections, the service, and a firewall rule. The test user gets in
   141:     # because it is a member of "Remote Desktop Users" (see vars above).
   142:     - name: Allow Remote Desktop connections
   143:       ansible.windows.win_regedit:
   144:         path: HKLM:\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server
   145:         name: fDenyTSConnections
   146:         data: 0
   147:         type: dword
   148:       when: windows_test_enable_rdp
   149: 
   150:     - name: Start the Remote Desktop service
   151:       ansible.windows.win_service:
   152:         name: TermService
   153:         start_mode: auto
   154:         state: started
   155:       when: windows_test_enable_rdp
   156: 
   157:     - name: Open the firewall for Remote Desktop
   158:       community.windows.win_firewall_rule:
   159:         name: Remote Desktop (managed by Ansible)
   160:         direction: in
   161:         action: allow
   162:         protocol: tcp
   163:         localport: "3389"
   164:         profiles:
   165:           - domain
   166:           - private
   167:           # Fresh workgroup/KubeVirt VMs classify the NIC as Public, so
   168:           # RDP stays blocked without this (lab-only; see README).
   169:           - public
   170:         state: present
   171:         enabled: true
   172:       when: windows_test_enable_rdp
   173: 
   174:     - name: Summarize what was provisioned
   175:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   176:         msg:
   177:           - "Test user:  {{ windows_test_user }} (groups: {{ windows_test_user_groups | join(', ') }})"
   178:           - "Apps:       {{ windows_test_apps | map(attribute='name') | join(', ') }}"
   179:           - "Extra pkgs: {{ windows_test_msi_packages | length }}"
   180:           - "RDP:        {{ 'enabled' if windows_test_enable_rdp else 'left as-is' }}"

name: playbooks/grafana-kiosk/setup-kiosk.yaml
review_question: Would an Ansible expert judge this playbook or task file as needing abstraction because it contains too many direct leaf tasks?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Grafana kiosk convergence - local auth proxy, memory/SD tuning, and the
     3: # browser/display stack. Provisions a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W (or any
     4: # Debian-family host) from a stock Raspberry Pi OS Lite install into a
     5: # boot-to-dashboard Grafana kiosk.
     6: #
     7: # Browser stacks (kiosk_stack):
     8: #   cog      - WPE WebKit rendering straight to DRM/KMS; no X server, no
     9: #              compositor. Lightest option for a 512MB board. DEFAULT.
    10: #   chromium - minimal X11 (xinit + openbox) with grafana/grafana-kiosk
    11: #              driving Chromium. Proven fallback if WPE misrenders a
    12: #              dashboard. Switching kiosk_stack retires the other stack's
    13: #              service automatically.
    14: #
    15: # Both stacks browse http://127.0.0.1:<port>, where a local nginx injects
    16: # `Authorization: Bearer <service-account token>` and proxies to Grafana -
    17: # the token lives in exactly one root-only file and the browser stays dumb.
    18: # Grafana's kiosk/playlist/refresh features are all URL parameters, so no
    19: # client-side login automation is needed on either stack.
    20: #
    21: # Required in host_vars: kiosk_grafana_url (e.g. https://grafana.example.com)
    22: # Secrets: the Grafana service-account token resolves from 1Password on the
    23: # controller (kiosk_grafana_token_op_*); CI/molecule passes an explicit
    24: # kiosk_grafana_token instead.
    25: - name: Grafana kiosk convergence - proxy, tuning, browser stack
    26:   hosts: "{{ ansible_limit | default('grafana_kiosk') }}"
    27:   become: true
    28:   gather_facts: true
    29: 
    30:   vars:
    31:     # Effective values; inventory overrides the un-prefixed names (play vars
    32:     # outrank inventory, hence the default() merge pattern).
    33:     _kiosk_stack: "{{ kiosk_stack | default('cog') }}"
    34:     _kiosk_user: "{{ kiosk_user | default('kiosk') }}"
    35:     _kiosk_proxy_listen: "{{ kiosk_proxy_listen | default('127.0.0.1:8480') }}"
    36:     _kiosk_proxy_base: "http://{{ _kiosk_proxy_listen }}"
    37:     # Dashboard or playlist path, e.g. '/playlists/play/<uid>' or
    38:     # '/d/<uid>/<slug>?orgId=1&refresh=30s'. The cog stack appends Grafana's
    39:     # kiosk URL param itself; grafana-kiosk adds it via kiosk-mode.
    40:     _kiosk_dashboard_path: "{{ kiosk_dashboard_path | default('/') }}"
    41:     # Append Grafana's kiosk param unless the query already carries a
    42:     # `kiosk` KEY (a value merely containing "kiosk", e.g. ?var-svc=kiosk,
    43:     # must not suppress it). Fragments in the path are unsupported.
    44:     _kiosk_dashboard_query: "{{ _kiosk_dashboard_path | urlsplit('query') }}"
    45:     _kiosk_cog_url: >-
    46:       {{ _kiosk_proxy_base ~ _kiosk_dashboard_path
    47:          ~ ('' if _kiosk_dashboard_query is search('(^|&)kiosk(=|&|$)')
    48:             else ('&kiosk' if _kiosk_dashboard_query else '?kiosk')) }}
    49:     # Explicit token wins (molecule/CI); otherwise kiosk_grafana_token_lookup
    50:     # — the full 1Password lookup expression carried in host_vars. default()
    51:     # keeps it lazy so container runs never touch 1Password.
    52:     _kiosk_grafana_token: "{{ kiosk_grafana_token | default(kiosk_grafana_token_lookup) }}"
    53:     # Chromium leaks on live dashboards (OOM within 6-8h on 512MB boards is
    54:     # widely reported); RuntimeMaxSec + Restart=always recycles the whole
    55:     # browser session daily before it gets there.
    56:     _kiosk_service_max_runtime: "{{ kiosk_service_max_runtime | default('24h') }}"
    57:     _kiosk_zram_size: "{{ kiosk_zram_size | default('ram / 2') }}"
    58:     _kiosk_gpu_mem: "{{ kiosk_gpu_mem | default(96) }}"
    59:     _kiosk_unit: "{{ 'cog-kiosk.service' if _kiosk_stack == 'cog' else 'grafana-kiosk.service' }}"
    60:     _kiosk_other_unit: "{{ 'grafana-kiosk.service' if _kiosk_stack == 'cog' else 'cog-kiosk.service' }}"
    61:     # Containers (molecule) have no kernel knobs, DRM, or display: install
    62:     # and enable everything, but skip zram/sysctl and service starts.
    63:     _kiosk_is_container: >-
    64:       {{ ansible_virtualization_type | default('')
    65:          in ['container', 'podman', 'docker', 'lxc', 'containerd'] }}
    66:     # Whether to start (and verify) the browser service. Defaults to "not a
    67:     # container", but headless guests without DRM/display (cloud-kernel
    68:     # molecule VMs, a Pi staged without a monitor) set kiosk_start_browser:
    69:     # false - the unit stays enabled and starts on next boot with a display.
    70:     _kiosk_start_browser: "{{ kiosk_start_browser | default(not _kiosk_is_container) }}"
    71:     # Extra Environment= lines for the cog unit (VM render testing; empty on
    72:     # real hardware - see README).
    73:     _kiosk_cog_env: "{{ kiosk_cog_env | default({}) }}"
    74:     # grafana-kiosk release pinning (chromium stack). Upstream publishes no
    75:     # checksums file, so sha256s are computed from the release assets and
    76:     # pinned here per version/arch. Extend the map when bumping the version.
    77:     _kiosk_gk_version: "{{ kiosk_grafana_kiosk_version | default('1.0.12') }}"
    78:     _kiosk_gk_arch: >-
    79:       {{ {'x86_64': 'amd64',
    80:           'aarch64': 'arm64',
    81:           'armv7l': 'armv7'}[ansible_architecture] }}
    82:     _kiosk_gk_checksums:
    83:       "1.0.12":
    84:         arm64: 8a3a8553d98ac91563677b3660c4d962bb5582c5d4f9c5cb3a0742cae8e49e47
    85:         amd64: 3bd8f535149e98b7ef72110fa1020963d5da0b97602cd232a0766f0554905696
    86:         armv7: cdc139752a48d4b4e197db3fcca9ca34af6de027ed8072ca1aadeb613c2e255d
    87: 
    88:   tasks:
    89:     - name: Validate kiosk configuration
    90:       ansible.builtin.assert:
    91:         that:
    92:           - kiosk_grafana_url is defined
    93:           - _kiosk_stack in ['cog', 'chromium']
    94:           - _kiosk_cog_env is mapping
    95:         fail_msg: >-
    96:           Set kiosk_grafana_url (e.g. https://grafana.example.com) in
    97:           host_vars, kiosk_stack to 'cog' or 'chromium', and kiosk_cog_env
    98:           (if set) to a dict of VAR: value pairs.
    99: 
   100:     # video/input are static base groups and render normally comes from
   101:     # udev, but molecule's slim containers lack it - ensure all three.
   102:     - name: Ensure display/input groups exist
   103:       ansible.builtin.group:
   104:         name: "{{ item }}"
   105:         state: present
   106:         system: true
   107:       loop:
   108:         - video
   109:         - render
   110:         - input
   111: 
   112:     - name: Create the kiosk user
   113:       ansible.builtin.user:
   114:         name: "{{ _kiosk_user }}"
   115:         groups:
   116:           - video
   117:           - render
   118:           - input
   119:         append: true
   120:         shell: /usr/sbin/nologin
   121:         create_home: true
   122:         password_lock: true
   123:         system: false
   124:         state: present
   125: 
   126:     - name: Install proxy and tuning packages
   127:       ansible.builtin.apt:
   128:         name:
   129:           - nginx-light
   130:           - systemd-zram-generator
   131:           - fonts-dejavu-core
   132:         state: present
   133:         install_recommends: false
   134:         update_cache: true
   135:         cache_valid_time: 3600
   136: 
   137:     - name: Create journald drop-in directory
   138:       ansible.builtin.file:
   139:         path: /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d
   140:         state: directory
   141:         owner: root
   142:         group: root
   143:         mode: "0755"
   144: 
   145:     - name: Keep journald off the SD card (volatile, capped)
   146:       ansible.builtin.copy:
   147:         dest: /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/50-grafana-kiosk.conf
   148:         content: |
   149:           # Managed by playbooks/grafana-kiosk/setup-kiosk.yaml
   150:           [Journal]
   151:           Storage=volatile
   152:           RuntimeMaxUse=32M
   153:         owner: root
   154:         group: root
   155:         mode: "0644"
   156:       notify: Restart journald
   157: 
   158:     - name: Configure zram swap (zstd)
   159:       ansible.builtin.template:
   160:         src: templates/zram-generator.conf.j2
   161:         dest: /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf
   162:         owner: root
   163:         group: root
   164:         mode: "0644"
   165:       notify: Restart zram swap
   166: 
   167:     # Activate zram now, not at end-of-play handler time: the browser stack
   168:     # install below unpacks Chromium-sized debs, and a first converge on a
   169:     # 512MB board needs the swap headroom already in place.
   170:     - name: Activate zram swap
   171:       ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
   172:         name: systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service
   173:         state: started
   174:         daemon_reload: true
   175:       when: not _kiosk_is_container
   176:

   192:         label: "{{ item.name }}"

   209:     - name: Template the auth-injecting Grafana proxy (holds the SA token)
   210:       ansible.builtin.template:
   211:         src: templates/grafana-proxy.conf.j2
   212:         dest: /etc/nginx/sites-available/grafana-kiosk.conf

   221:         src: /etc/nginx/sites-available/grafana-kiosk.conf
   222:         dest: /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/grafana-kiosk.conf
   223:         state: link
   224:       notify: Reload nginx
   225: 
   226:     - name: Remove the default nginx site
   227:       ansible.builtin.file:
   228:         path: /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default
   229:         state: absent
   230:       notify: Reload nginx

   232:     - name: Enable and start nginx
   233:       ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
   234:         name: nginx.service

   236:         state: started
   237: 
   238:     - name: Include browser stack tasks - {{ _kiosk_stack }}
   239:       ansible.builtin.include_tasks: "stack_tasks/_stack_{{ _kiosk_stack }}.yml"
   240: 
   241:     # Clean stack switching: if the other stack was deployed before, retire
   242:     # its service so two browsers never fight over the display.

   255:     - name: Apply pending restarts before verifying

   257: 
   258:     # Verification goes through the proxy, so a 200 proves nginx, upstream

   287:           {{ ansible_facts.services[_kiosk_unit] | default('unit not found') }}

   299:         state: restarted
   300:         daemon_reload: true
   301:       when: not _kiosk_is_container

   303:     - name: Reload nginx
   304:       ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
   305:         name: nginx.service
   306:         state: reloaded

   308:     - name: Restart kiosk service

source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Add worker nodes to an existing OpenShift cluster by generating PXE
     3: # boot artifacts via `oc adm node-image create --pxe` and copying them
     4: # into the TrueNAS public nginx docroot (served at
     5: # https://public.igou.systems/boot-files/). Post-2026-05-11: the
     6: # netbootxyz container is retired; public nginx owns assets and rb5009
     7: # flash owns per-host pins.
     8: #
     9: # Source procedure:
    10: #   https://github.com/openshift/openshift-docs/blob/main/nodes/nodes/nodes-nodes-adding-node-iso.adoc
    11: #
    12: # What this playbook owns:
    13: #   /mnt/ssd/public/boot-files/<cluster>-add-node/
    14: #     node.<arch>-vmlinuz, node.<arch>-initrd.img, node.<arch>-rootfs.img
    15: #
    16: # What this playbook does NOT own (deploy_assets.yml owns it):
    17: #   the per-host iPXE pin (MAC-<hex>.ipxe) on rb5009 flash
    18: #
    19: # The per-host iPXE script that points iPXE at the boot artifacts is
    20: # rendered by playbooks/netboot/deploy_assets.yml from inventory's
    21: # netboot_host_pins. The operator maintains the pin entry there;
    22: # add_node_iso.yml only refreshes the boot artifacts (kernel/initrd/
    23: # rootfs) when invoked. The artifacts behind the URL rotate (token
    24: # embedded in initrd has limited lifetime); the pin file stays stable.
    25: #
    26: # Operator workflow (initial):
    27: #   1. Add worker(s) to inventory under group `openshift_workers_<cluster>`
    28: #      with at minimum `openshift_add_node_mac`. Add
    29: #      `openshift_add_node_network_config` (nmstate) for static IPs.
    30: #   2. Add a netboot_host_pins entry for the worker MAC in
    31: #      igou-inventory/group_vars/all/netboot.yml. The pin's iPXE script
    32: #      should reference {{ netboot_public_url }}/<cluster>-add-node/{vmlinuz,
    33: #      initrd.img,rootfs.img} (e.g. as a menu option, or directly).
    34: #   3. Set on the cluster host (e.g., host_vars/ocp.yml):
    35: #        openshift_add_node_arch: x86_64
    36: #        openshift_add_node_boot_artifacts_base_url: {{ netboot_public_url }}/<cluster>-add-node/
    37: #   4. Deploy the pin once:
    38: #        ansible-playbook playbooks/netboot/deploy_assets.yml \
    39: #          -i igou-inventory/inventory.yaml --tags render,push,verify
    40: #   5. export KUBECONFIG=<path-to-cluster-kubeconfig>
    41: #   6. Generate / refresh the boot artifacts:
    42: #        ansible-playbook playbooks/openshift/add_node_iso.yml \
    43: #          -i igou-inventory/inventory.yaml -e target_cluster=<cluster>
    44: #   7. PXE-boot the worker.
    45: #   8. Optionally: re-run with `--tags monitor` to watch the join.
    46: #   9. Approve any pending CSRs manually:
    47: #        oc get csr
    48: #        oc adm certificate approve <name>
    49: #
    50: # Operator workflow (subsequent runs, e.g. token refresh):
    51: #   Steps 5-9 only. The pin file stays in place; just refresh the
    52: #   artifacts behind the URL.
    53: 
    54: - name: Generate OpenShift add-node PXE assets
    55:   # target_cluster selects the cluster + its worker group; it defaults to
    56:   # ocp when not passed via -e. _cluster materializes that default as a
    57:   # real variable so every reference below resolves (a bare
    58:   # `target_cluster | default(...)` on the hosts line alone does NOT define
    59:   # the variable for the rest of the play). The pre_tasks still fail fast
    60:   # if the resulting worker group is empty or a worker is missing its MAC.
    61:   hosts: "{{ target_cluster | default('ocp') }}"
    62:   connection: local
    63:   gather_facts: true
    64:   vars:
    65:     _cluster: "{{ target_cluster | default('ocp') }}"
    66:     openshift_add_node_work_dir: "{{ ansible_env.HOME }}/openshift-add-node/{{ _cluster }}"
    67:   pre_tasks:
    68:     - name: Preflight — KUBECONFIG must be set in the environment
    69:       ansible.builtin.assert:
    70:         that:
    71:           - lookup('env', 'KUBECONFIG') | length > 0
    72:         fail_msg: >-
    73:           KUBECONFIG environment variable is not set. Export it before
    74:           running this playbook (e.g., `export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/ocp-config`).
    75: 
    76:     - name: Preflight — worker group must exist and be non-empty
    77:       vars:
    78:         _workers_group: "openshift_workers_{{ _cluster }}"
    79:         _workers: "{{ groups[_workers_group] | default([]) }}"
    80:       ansible.builtin.assert:
    81:         that:
    82:           - _workers | length > 0
    83:         fail_msg: >-
    84:           Inventory group `{{ _workers_group }}` is missing or empty.
    85:           Add at least one worker host to that group with
    86:           `openshift_add_node_mac` set.
    87: 
    88:     - name: Preflight — every worker must have a valid MAC address
    89:       ansible.builtin.assert:
    90:         that:
    91:           - hostvars[item].openshift_add_node_mac is defined
    92:           - hostvars[item].openshift_add_node_mac | default('') is match('^([0-9A-Fa-f]{2}[:-]){5}[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}$')
    93:         fail_msg: >-
    94:           Worker `{{ item }}` is missing or has an invalid
    95:           `openshift_add_node_mac`. Expected format aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff.
    96:       loop: "{{ groups['openshift_workers_' + _cluster] }}"
    97:       loop_control:
    98:         label: "{{ item }}"
    99: 
   100:     - name: Preflight — discover nodes already joined to the cluster
   101:       ansible.builtin.command:
   102:         cmd: oc get nodes -o jsonpath={.items[*].metadata.name}
   103:       register: _existing_nodes
   104:       changed_when: false
   105: 
   106:     - name: Preflight — compute pending workers (in group, not yet joined)
   107:       # oc adm node-image create rejects any host already present as a
   108:       # cluster node ("hostname conflict"). Render only the workers that
   109:       # haven't joined yet, matching on both FQDN and short name.
   110:       vars:
   111:         _joined: "{{ _existing_nodes.stdout.split() }}"
   112:         _joined_short: "{{ _existing_nodes.stdout.split() | map('regex_replace', '[.].*$', '') | list }}"
   113:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   114:         _pending_workers: >-
   115:           {{ groups['openshift_workers_' + _cluster]
   116:              | reject('in', _joined + _joined_short)
   117:              | list }}
   118: 
   119:     - name: Preflight — at least one worker must be pending
   120:       ansible.builtin.assert:
   121:         that:
   122:           - _pending_workers | length > 0
   123:         success_msg: "Pending worker(s) to add: {{ _pending_workers | join(', ') }}"
   124:         fail_msg: >-
   125:           Every host in openshift_workers_{{ _cluster }} is already a node in
   126:           the cluster ({{ _existing_nodes.stdout.split() | join(', ') }}).
   127:           Nothing to add — add a new worker to the group first.
   128: 
   129:   tasks:
   130:     - name: Wipe stale work dir
   131:       ansible.builtin.file:
   132:         path: "{{ openshift_add_node_work_dir }}"
   133:         state: absent
   134: 
   135:     - name: Create fresh work dir
   136:       ansible.builtin.file:
   137:         path: "{{ openshift_add_node_work_dir }}"
   138:         state: directory
   139:         mode: "0700"
   140: 
   141:     - name: Fetch cluster pull secret to work dir
   142:       ansible.builtin.shell: |
   143:         set -o pipefail
   144:         oc -n openshift-config get secret pull-secret \
   145:           -o jsonpath='{.data.\.dockerconfigjson}' \
   146:           | base64 -d > "{{ openshift_add_node_work_dir }}/auth.json"
   147:       args:
   148:         executable: /bin/bash
   149:       changed_when: true
   150:       no_log: true
   151: 
   152:     - name: Lock down pull secret file mode
   153:       ansible.builtin.file:
   154:         path: "{{ openshift_add_node_work_dir }}/auth.json"
   155:         mode: "0600"
   156: 
   157:     - name: Render nodes-config.yaml
   158:       ansible.builtin.template:
   159:         src: templates/nodes-config.yaml.j2
   160:         dest: "{{ openshift_add_node_work_dir }}/nodes-config.yaml"
   161:         mode: "0644"
   162: 
   163:     - name: Run `oc adm node-image create --pxe`
   164:       # work_dir is wiped above, so this always runs and always produces fresh
   165:       # assets; changed_when reflects that.
   166:       ansible.builtin.command:
   167:         cmd: >-
   168:           oc adm node-image create --pxe
   169:           --dir {{ openshift_add_node_work_dir }}
   170:           --registry-config {{ openshift_add_node_work_dir }}/auth.json
   171:       changed_when: true
   172: 
   173:     - name: List generated PXE assets
   174:       ansible.builtin.find:
   175:         paths: "{{ openshift_add_node_work_dir }}"
   176:         file_type: file
   177:         excludes:
   178:           - auth.json
   179:           - nodes-config.yaml
   180:       register: _add_node_assets
   181: 
   182:     - name: Show generated PXE asset filenames
   183:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   184:         msg: "{{ _add_node_assets.files | map(attribute='path') | map('basename') | sort }}"
   185: 
   186:     - name: Verify expected PXE asset files exist
   187:       ansible.builtin.stat:
   188:         path: "{{ openshift_add_node_work_dir }}/{{ item }}"
   189:       register: _asset_stat
   190:       failed_when: not _asset_stat.stat.exists
   191:       loop:
   192:         - "node.{{ openshift_add_node_arch }}.ipxe"
   193:         - "node.{{ openshift_add_node_arch }}-vmlinuz"
   194:         - "node.{{ openshift_add_node_arch }}-initrd.img"
   195:         - "node.{{ openshift_add_node_arch }}-rootfs.img"
   196:       loop_control:
   197:         label: "{{ item }}"
   198: 
   199:     - name: Set fact for Play 2 — generated asset paths
   200:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   201:         openshift_add_node_pxe_assets:
   202:           ipxe: "{{ openshift_add_node_work_dir }}/node.{{ openshift_add_node_arch }}.ipxe"
   203:           work_dir: "{{ openshift_add_node_work_dir }}"
   204:           arch: "{{ openshift_add_node_arch }}"
   205: 
   206:     - name: Monitor add-node progress
   207:       # `oc adm node-image monitor` skips CSR-readiness checks if reverse DNS
   208:       # is not available for a node IP. CSR approval is always manual (see
   209:       # operator workflow step 7) regardless of whether monitor completes.
   210:       tags: [monitor, never]
   211:       vars:
   212:         _worker_ips: >-
   213:           {{ groups['openshift_workers_' + _cluster]
   214:              | map('extract', hostvars)
   215:              | map(attribute='openshift_add_node_network_config', default={})
   216:              | map(attribute='interfaces', default=[])
   217:              | map(attribute='0', default={})
   218:              | map(attribute='ipv4', default={})
   219:              | map(attribute='address', default=[])
   220:              | map(attribute='0', default={})
   221:              | map(attribute='ip', default='')
   222:              | list }}
   223:       block:
   224:         - name: Assert every worker has a static IP for monitoring
   225:           ansible.builtin.assert:
   226:             that:
   227:               - _worker_ips | reject('equalto', '') | list | length == _worker_ips | length
   228:             fail_msg: >-
   229:               At least one worker has no static IP in
   230:               `openshift_add_node_network_config`. Run
   231:               `oc adm node-image monitor --ip-addresses <ips>` manually
   232:               with addresses discovered from DHCP.
   233: 
   234:         - name: Run `oc adm node-image monitor`
   235:           ansible.builtin.command:
   236:             cmd: >-
   237:               oc adm node-image monitor
   238:               --ip-addresses {{ _worker_ips | join(',') }}
   239:           changed_when: false
   240: 
   241: - name: Deliver PXE assets to TrueNAS public nginx
   242:   hosts: truenas
   243:   become: true
   244:   gather_facts: false
   245:   vars:
   246:     _cluster: "{{ target_cluster | default('ocp') }}"
   247:     cluster_host: "{{ _cluster }}"
   248:     # Read via the fact set by Play 1's set_fact task; play-level vars are
   249:     # not promoted into hostvars across plays, but set_fact values are.
   250:     work_dir: "{{ hostvars[cluster_host]['openshift_add_node_pxe_assets']['work_dir'] }}"
   251:     arch: "{{ hostvars[cluster_host]['openshift_add_node_pxe_assets']['arch'] }}"
   252:     truenas_assets_root: /mnt/ssd/public/boot-files
   253:     asset_subdir: "{{ cluster_host }}-add-node"
   254:   tasks:
   255:     - name: Ensure asset destination directory exists
   256:       ansible.builtin.file:
   257:         path: "{{ truenas_assets_root }}/{{ asset_subdir }}"
   258:         state: directory
   259:         mode: "0755"
   260:         owner: "950"
   261:         group: "950"
   262: 
   263:     - name: Sync boot artifacts to TrueNAS
   264:       ansible.posix.synchronize:
   265:         src: "{{ work_dir }}/"
   266:         dest: "{{ truenas_assets_root }}/{{ asset_subdir }}/"
   267:         delete: true
   268:         rsync_opts:
   269:           - "--exclude=*.ipxe"
   270:           - "--exclude=auth.json"
   271:           - "--exclude=nodes-config.yaml"
   272:           - "--chown=950:950"
   273:           # Force world-readable files + world-traversable dirs so the public
   274:           # nginx worker can serve them regardless of its runtime UID. Mirrors
   275:           # playbooks/netboot/tasks/push_text.yml; without this the synced tree
   276:           # kept perms the nginx worker could not read -> HTTP 403 -> the iPXE
   277:           # pin's initrd fetch failed and the boot menu silently exited.
   278:           - "--chmod=F0644,D0755"

    28:     validate_certs: true
    29:     use_proxy: false
    30:     ca_path: "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_controller_ca_path }}"
    31:     status_code: 200
    32:     timeout: "{{ vault_raft_snapshot_timeout }}"
    33:   loop: "{{ vault_raft_snapshot_verification_kv_paths }}"
    34:   register: _vault_raft_snapshot_kv_documents
    35:   delegate_to: "{{ vault_raft_snapshot_api_delegate_to }}"
    36:   become: false
    37:   changed_when: false
    38:   no_log: true
    39: 
    40: - name: Initialize Raft snapshot verification records
    41:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    42:     _vault_raft_snapshot_verification_records: []
    43:   changed_when: false
    44:   no_log: true
    45: 
    46: - name: Build non-secret Raft snapshot KV identities
    47:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    48:     _vault_raft_snapshot_verification_records: >-
    49:       {{
    50:         _vault_raft_snapshot_verification_records
    51:         + [
    52:             {
    53:               'mount_point': item.item.mount_point,
    54:               'path': item.item.path,
    55:               'document_sha256': (
    56:                 item.json.data.data
    57:                 | to_json(sort_keys=true, separators=[',', ':'])
    58:                 | hash('sha256')
    59:               )
    60:             }
    61:           ]
    62:       }}
    63:   loop: "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_kv_documents.results }}"
    64:   changed_when: false
    65:   no_log: true
    66: 
    67: - name: Allocate a protected controller Raft snapshot directory
    68:   ansible.builtin.tempfile:
    69:     state: directory
    70:     path: /tmp
    71:     prefix: lit-vault-raft-snapshot-
    72:   register: _vault_raft_snapshot_tempdir
    73:   delegate_to: "{{ vault_raft_snapshot_api_delegate_to }}"

    75:   changed_when: false
    76:   no_log: true
    77: 
    78: - name: Capture and escrow the production Raft snapshot
    79:   no_log: true
    80:   block:
    81:     - name: Enforce owner-only controller snapshot directory mode
    82:       ansible.builtin.file:
    83:         path: "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_tempdir.path }}"
    84:         state: directory
    85:         mode: "0700"
    86:       delegate_to: "{{ vault_raft_snapshot_api_delegate_to }}"
