    88:       changed_when: false
    89: 
    90:     - name: Download the production Vault Raft snapshot

    95:           X-Vault-Token: "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_login.json.auth.client_token }}"
    96:         validate_certs: true
    97:         use_proxy: false
    98:         ca_path: "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_controller_ca_path }}"
    99:         status_code: 200
   100:         timeout: "{{ vault_raft_snapshot_timeout }}"
   101:         dest: "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_tempdir.path }}/vault.snap"
   102:         return_content: false
   103:       delegate_to: "{{ vault_raft_snapshot_api_delegate_to }}"
   104:       become: false
   105:       changed_when: false
   106: 
   107:     - name: Enforce owner-only raw snapshot mode
   108:       ansible.builtin.file:
   109:         path: "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_tempdir.path }}/vault.snap"
   110:         state: file
   111:         mode: "0600"
   112:       delegate_to: "{{ vault_raft_snapshot_api_delegate_to }}"
   113:       become: false
   114:       changed_when: false
   115: 
   116:     - name: Calculate raw Raft snapshot identity
   117:       ansible.builtin.stat:
   118:         path: "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_tempdir.path }}/vault.snap"
   119:         follow: false
   120:         get_checksum: true
   121:         checksum_algorithm: sha256
   122:         get_attributes: false
   123:         get_mime: false
   124:       register: _vault_raft_snapshot_raw_stat
   125:       delegate_to: "{{ vault_raft_snapshot_api_delegate_to }}"
   126:       become: false
   127:       changed_when: false
   128: 
   129:     - name: Require a safe owner-only raw Raft snapshot
   130:       ansible.builtin.assert:
   131:         that:
   132:           - _vault_raft_snapshot_raw_stat.stat.exists | default(false)
   133:           - _vault_raft_snapshot_raw_stat.stat.isreg | default(false)
   134:           - not (_vault_raft_snapshot_raw_stat.stat.islnk | default(false))
   135:           - _vault_raft_snapshot_raw_stat.stat.nlink | int == 1
   136:           - _vault_raft_snapshot_raw_stat.stat.mode == '0600'
   137:           - _vault_raft_snapshot_raw_stat.stat.size | int > 0
   138:           - >-
   139:             _vault_raft_snapshot_raw_stat.stat.checksum
   140:             is match('^[0-9a-f]{64}$')
   141:         fail_msg: "Raw Vault Raft snapshot is missing, unsafe, or empty."
   142:         quiet: true
   143: 
   144:     - name: Report the non-secret raw Raft snapshot size contract
   145:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   146:         msg: >-
   147:           Raw Vault Raft snapshot size is
   148:           {{ _vault_raft_snapshot_raw_stat.stat.size | int }} bytes; the
   149:           approved limit is {{ vault_raft_snapshot_max_raw_bytes | int }} bytes.
   150:       no_log: false
   151: 
   152:     - name: Require the raw Raft snapshot within the approved size bound
   153:       ansible.builtin.assert:
   154:         that:
   155:           - >-
   156:             _vault_raft_snapshot_raw_stat.stat.size | int
   157:             <= vault_raft_snapshot_max_raw_bytes | int
   158:         fail_msg: >-
   159:           Raw Vault Raft snapshot exceeds the approved
   160:           {{ vault_raft_snapshot_max_raw_bytes | int }}-byte limit.
   161:         quiet: true
   162:       no_log: false
   163: 
   164:     - name: Read the raw Raft snapshot into protected Ansible memory
   165:       ansible.builtin.slurp:
   166:         src: "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_tempdir.path }}/vault.snap"
   167:       register: _vault_raft_snapshot_raw
   168:       delegate_to: "{{ vault_raft_snapshot_api_delegate_to }}"
   169:       become: false
   170:       changed_when: false
   171: 
   172:     - name: Build the encrypted Raft snapshot escrow document
   173:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   174:         # Build the whole mapping in one native expression. Templating a
   175:         # dynamic scalar inside a YAML mapping stringifies it on controllers
   176:         # that disable Jinja native types.
   177:         _vault_raft_snapshot_document: >-
   178:           {{
   179:             {
   180:               'schema_version': 1,
   181:               'subject': vault_raft_snapshot_document_subject,
   182:               'storage_backend': 'raft',
   183:               'image': vault_raft_snapshot_image,
   184:               'cluster_id': _vault_raft_snapshot_health.json.cluster_id,
   185:               'snapshot_sha256': _vault_raft_snapshot_raw_stat.stat.checksum,
   186:               'snapshot_size_bytes': _vault_raft_snapshot_raw_stat.stat.size | int,
   187:               'snapshot_b64': _vault_raft_snapshot_raw.content,
   188:               'verification_records': _vault_raft_snapshot_verification_records
   189:             }
   190:           }}
   191:       changed_when: false
   192: 
   193:     - name: Persist immutable encrypted off-host Raft snapshot escrow
   194:       lit.foundational.ansible_vault_document:
   195:         path: "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_document_path }}"
   196:         document: "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_document }}"
   197:       register: _vault_raft_snapshot_escrow_result
   198:       delegate_to: "{{ vault_raft_snapshot_api_delegate_to }}"
   199:       become: false
   200:       no_log: true
   201: 
   202:     - name: Revalidate exact encrypted off-host Raft snapshot escrow
   203:       lit.foundational.ansible_vault_document:
   204:         path: "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_document_path }}"
   205:         document: "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_document }}"
   206:       delegate_to: "{{ vault_raft_snapshot_api_delegate_to }}"
   207:       become: false
   208:       no_log: true
   209: 
   210:     - name: Inspect encrypted off-host Raft snapshot escrow
   211:       ansible.builtin.stat:
   212:         path: "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_document_path }}"
   213:         follow: false
   214:         get_checksum: true
   215:         checksum_algorithm: sha256
   216:         get_attributes: false
   217:         get_mime: false
   218:       register: _vault_raft_snapshot_ciphertext_stat
   219:       delegate_to: "{{ vault_raft_snapshot_api_delegate_to }}"
   220:       become: false
   221:       changed_when: false
   222: 
   223:     - name: Read only the Raft snapshot ciphertext signature
   224:       ansible.builtin.command:
   225:         argv:
   226:           - head
   227:           - -c
   228:           - "15"
   229:           - "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_document_path }}"
   230:       register: _vault_raft_snapshot_ciphertext_signature
   231:       delegate_to: "{{ vault_raft_snapshot_api_delegate_to }}"
   232:       become: false
   233:       changed_when: false
   234:       check_mode: false
   235: 
   236:     - name: Require safe Ansible Vault ciphertext for Raft snapshot escrow
   237:       ansible.builtin.assert:
   238:         that:
   239:           - _vault_raft_snapshot_ciphertext_stat.stat.exists | default(false)
   240:           - _vault_raft_snapshot_ciphertext_stat.stat.isreg | default(false)
   241:           - not (_vault_raft_snapshot_ciphertext_stat.stat.islnk | default(false))
   242:           - _vault_raft_snapshot_ciphertext_stat.stat.nlink | int == 1
   243:           - >-
   244:             _vault_raft_snapshot_ciphertext_stat.stat.uid | int
   245:             in [0, _vault_raft_snapshot_controller_uid | int]
   246:           - _vault_raft_snapshot_ciphertext_stat.stat.mode in ['0400', '0600']
   247:           - _vault_raft_snapshot_ciphertext_stat.stat.size | int > 0
   248:           - >-
   249:             _vault_raft_snapshot_ciphertext_stat.stat.size | int
   250:             <= vault_raft_snapshot_max_raw_bytes | int * 4
   251:           - >-
   252:             _vault_raft_snapshot_ciphertext_stat.stat.checksum
   253:             is match('^[0-9a-f]{64}$')
   254:           - _vault_raft_snapshot_ciphertext_signature.stdout == '$ANSIBLE_VAULT;'
   255:         fail_msg: >-
   256:           Raft snapshot escrow is not safe owner-only Ansible Vault ciphertext.
   257:         quiet: true
   258: 
   259:     - name: Record safe Raft snapshot escrow identity
   260:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   261:         vault_raft_snapshot_escrow_verified: true
   262:         vault_raft_snapshot_escrow_path: "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_document_path }}"
   263:         vault_raft_snapshot_escrow_ciphertext_sha256: >-
   264:           {{ _vault_raft_snapshot_ciphertext_stat.stat.checksum }}
   265:         vault_raft_snapshot_raw_sha256: "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_raw_stat.stat.checksum }}"
   266:         vault_raft_snapshot_raw_size_bytes: "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_raw_stat.stat.size | int }}"
   267:       changed_when: false
   268: 
   269:   always:
   270:     - name: Remove every raw controller Raft snapshot artifact
   271:       ansible.builtin.file:
   272:         path: "{{ _vault_raft_snapshot_tempdir.path }}"
   273:         state: absent
   274:       delegate_to: "{{ vault_raft_snapshot_api_delegate_to }}"
   275:       become: false
   276:       changed_when: false
   277:       no_log: true

     5:     - name: Create EFS

    14:                 aws_tags_role_efs_storage,

    27:             ]
    28:           })

    33:     - name: Set EFS LifeCycle Policies
    34:       when: efs_lifecycle_policies and efs_lifecycle_policies | length > 0
    35:       command: >-
    36:         aws efs put-lifecycle-configuration
    37:           --region '{{ aws_region }}'
    38:           --file-system-id '{{ _aws_efs.efs.file_system_id }}'
    39:           --lifecycle-policies '{{ efs_lifecycle_policies | to_json }}'
    40:

    42:   dnf:
    43:     name:
    44:         - stunnel
    45:         - nfs-utils
    46:         - "{{ efs_utils_package }}"
    47:     state: present
    48: 
    49: - name: Make sure root mount points exists
    50:   file:
    51:     path: "{{ efs_root_mountpoint }}"
    52:     state: directory
    53: 
    54: # EFS Once created takes a really long time to become available
    55: # hence the retries
    56: - name: Configure root mount
    57:   mount:
    58:     boot: yes
    59:     src: "{{ _aws_efs.efs.file_system_id }}:/"
    60:     path: "{{ efs_root_mountpoint }}"
    61:     fstype: efs
    62:     state: mounted
    63:     opts: "defaults,{{ efs_mount_opts }}"
    64:   register: efs_root_mount
    65:   until: efs_root_mount is not failed
    66:   retries: 300
    67:   delay: 30
    68: 
    69: - name: Make sure remote mount points exist with proper permissions
    70:   file:
    71:     path: "{{ efs_root_mountpoint }}{{ item.remote_path }}"
    72:     owner: "{{ item.owner | default('root') }}"
    73:     group: "{{ item.group | default('root') }}"
    74:     mode: 0770
    75:     state: directory
    76:   with_items: "{{ efs_mounts }}"
    77: 
    78: - name: Make sure local mount points exists
    79:   file:
    80:     path: "{{ item.local_mountpoint }}"
    81:     state: directory
    82:   with_items: "{{ efs_mounts }}"
    83: 
    84: - name: Check if target directories are already mounted
    85:   command: "mountpoint {{ item.local_mountpoint }}"
    86:   register: _efs_local_mountpoints
    87:   failed_when: no
    88:   changed_when: no
    89:   with_items: "{{ efs_mounts }}"
    90: 
    91: - name: Copy any preexisting files before we mount over these directories (but do not overwrite existing)
    92:   shell: "rsync --archive --ignore-existing {{ item[0].local_mountpoint }}/ {{ efs_root_mountpoint }}{{ item[0].remote_path }}/"
    93:   when: item[1].rc != 0
    94:   with_together:
    95:     - "{{ efs_mounts }}"
    96:     - "{{ _efs_local_mountpoints.results }}"
    97: 
    98: - name: Configure mounts
    99:   mount:
   100:     boot: yes
   101:     src: "{{ _aws_efs.efs.file_system_id }}:{{ item.remote_path }}"
   102:     path: "{{ item.local_mountpoint }}"
   103:     fstype: efs
   104:     state: mounted
   105:     opts: "defaults,{{ efs_mount_opts }}"
   106:   with_items: "{{ efs_mounts }}"
   107: 
   108: # Warning, this has to be done post-mount!
   109: - name: Ensure mount permissions
   110:   file:
   111:     path: "{{ item.local_mountpoint }}"
   112:     state: directory
   113:     owner: "{{ item.owner | default('root') }}"
   114:     group: "{{ item.group | default('root') }}"
   115:     mode: 0770
   116:   with_items: "{{ efs_mounts }}"
   117: 
   118: - name: Make sure EFS is always in case the filesystem it's mounted over disappears (S3FS?)
   119:   when: efs_mount_watchdog_cron_enable
   120:   cron:
   121:     name: "Ensure {{ item.local_mountpoint }} is mounted"
   122:     job: "/bin/bash -c 'mountpoint {{ item.local_mountpoint }} || mount {{ item.local_mountpoint }}'"
   123:   with_items: "{{ efs_mounts }}"

source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Process individual workload - spawn nbdkit on its hypervisor
     3: 
     4: - name: Get workload details
     5:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
     6:     instance_id: "{{ workload_item._info.id }}"
     7:     instance_name: "{{ workload_item.params.name }}"
     8:     instance_status: "{{ workload_item._info.status }}"
     9:     hypervisor_hostname: "{{ workload_item._info.hypervisor_hostname | default('') }}"
    10: 
    11: - name: Fail if instance is not SHUTOFF
    12:   ansible.builtin.fail:
    13:     msg: "Instance {{ instance_name }} ({{ instance_id }}) must be SHUTOFF. Current status: {{ instance_status }}"
    14:   when: instance_status != "SHUTOFF"
    15: 
    16: - name: Fail if hypervisor hostname not in workload data
    17:   ansible.builtin.fail:
    18:     msg: "Hypervisor hostname not found in workload data for {{ instance_name }}. Run export_workloads first."
    19:   when: hypervisor_hostname == ''
    20: 
    21: - name: Display workload info
    22:   ansible.builtin.debug:
    23:     msg:
    24:       - "Processing: {{ instance_name }}"
    25:       - "Instance ID: {{ instance_id }}"
    26:       - "Hypervisor: {{ hypervisor_hostname }}"
    27:       - "Status: {{ instance_status }}"
    28: 
    29: - name: Find all instance disks on hypervisor
    30:   ansible.builtin.raw: |
    31:     # Find disk, disk.eph0, disk.eph1, etc. but exclude disk.info
    32:     find {{ os_migrate_nbdkit_nova_instances_dir }}/{{ instance_id }} -name 'disk*' -type f ! -name '*.info' | sort
    33:   delegate_to: "{{ hypervisor_hostname }}"
    34:   register: disk_paths_result
    35:   changed_when: false
    36: 
    37: - name: Parse disk paths
    38:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    39:     instance_disk_paths: "{{ disk_paths_result.stdout_lines | select('match', '.*disk.*') | reject('search', 'disk.info') | list }}"
    40: 
    41: - name: Fail if no disks found
    42:   ansible.builtin.fail:
    43:     msg: "No disks found for instance {{ instance_id }} on hypervisor {{ hypervisor_hostname }}"
    44:   when: instance_disk_paths | length == 0
    45: 
    46: - name: Display found disks
    47:   ansible.builtin.debug:
    48:     msg: "Found {{ instance_disk_paths | length }} disk(s): {{ instance_disk_paths }}"
    49: 
    50: - name: Initialize nbdkit disk info list
    51:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    52:     nbdkit_disk_info: []
    53: 
    54: - name: Set base port for nbdkit
    55:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    56:     nbdkit_base_port: "{{ workload_item._migration_params.nbdkit_port | default(os_migrate_nbdkit_port) }}"
    57: 
    58: - name: Process each disk
    59:   ansible.builtin.include_tasks: process_disk.yml
    60:   loop: "{{ instance_disk_paths }}"
    61:   loop_control:
    62:     loop_var: disk_item
    63:     index_var: disk_loop_index
    64:     label: "{{ disk_item | basename }}"
    65:   vars:
    66:     disk_device_name: >-
    67:       {%- set disk_basename = disk_item | basename -%}
    68:       {%- if disk_basename == 'disk' -%}
    69:       /dev/vda
    70:       {%- elif 'disk.eph' in disk_basename -%}
    71:       /dev/vd{{ 'bcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'[disk_loop_index - 1] }}
    72:       {%- else -%}
    73:       /dev/vd{{ 'bcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'[disk_loop_index] }}
    74:       {%- endif -%}
    75:     disk_is_bootable: "{{ (disk_item | basename) == 'disk' }}"
    76: 
    77: 
    78: - name: Update workload with multiple nbdkit URIs
    79:   os_migrate.os_migrate.update_workload_nbdkit_uris:
    80:     path: "{{ os_migrate_data_dir }}/workloads.yml"
    81:     instance_id: "{{ instance_id }}"
    82:     nbdkit_disks: "{{ nbdkit_disk_info }}"
    83: 
    84: - name: Success message
    85:   ansible.builtin.debug:
    86:     msg:
    87:       - "Successfully spawned {{ nbdkit_disk_info | length }} nbdkit process(es) for {{ instance_name }}"
    88:       - "Disks: {{ nbdkit_disk_info | map(attribute='disk_name') | list }}"
    89:       - "Ports: {{ nbdkit_disk_info | map(attribute='port') | list }}"

   175:               delegate_to: localhost

     5:     - name: Check if systemd service exists
     6:       ansible.builtin.stat:
     7:         path: "/etc/systemd/system/{{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}.service"
     8:       register: service_file
     9: 
    10:     - name: Check if dashboard systemd unit exists
    11:       ansible.builtin.stat:
    12:         path: "/etc/systemd/system/{{ agent_type }}-dashboard-{{ agent_name }}.service"
    13:       register: dashboard_unit_file
    14: 
    15:     # PartOf would normally propagate stop from the gateway to the dashboard,
    16:     # but we want the dashboard down even if the gateway is already stopped
    17:     # (idempotent stop / disable). Stop dashboard FIRST so an in-flight
    18:     # request that races the gateway shutdown still completes against a live
    19:     # dashboard process.
    20:     - name: Stop hermes dashboard service gracefully
    21:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
    22:         name: "{{ agent_type }}-dashboard-{{ agent_name }}"
    23:         state: stopped
    24:       when: dashboard_unit_file.stat.exists
    25:       ignore_errors: yes
    26: 
    27:     - name: Disable hermes dashboard service
    28:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
    29:         name: "{{ agent_type }}-dashboard-{{ agent_name }}"
    30:         enabled: no
    31:       when: dashboard_unit_file.stat.exists
    32:       ignore_errors: yes
    33: 
    34:     - name: Stop hermes service gracefully
    35:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
    36:         name: "{{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}"
    37:         state: stopped
    38:       register: stop_result
    39:       when: service_file.stat.exists
    40:       ignore_errors: yes
    41: 
    42:     - name: Disable hermes service
    43:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
    44:         name: "{{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}"
    45:         enabled: no
    46:       when: service_file.stat.exists
    47:       ignore_errors: yes
    48: 
    49:     - name: Wait for service to stop
    50:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
    51:         name: "{{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}"
    52:       register: service_status
    53:       until: service_status.status.ActiveState != "active"
    54:       retries: 10
    55:       delay: 2
    56:       when: service_file.stat.exists
    57:       ignore_errors: yes
    58: 
    59:     # hermes is a Python application invoked as `python3 ... hermes gateway run`.
    60:     # A plain `pgrep -u <user> hermes` matches only the executable basename and
    61:     # will miss the python process even when the gateway is still running.
    62:     # Match against the full command line with `-f 'hermes gateway run'` so the
    63:     # check is meaningful regardless of the underlying interpreter.
    64:     - name: Verify hermes process is stopped
    65:       ansible.builtin.command:
    66:         cmd: pgrep -u {{ agent_name }} -f "hermes gateway run"
    67:       register: process_check
    68:       changed_when: false
    69:       failed_when: process_check.rc == 0

    72:     # (with its own node child process). The gateway pgrep above does not
    73:     # catch a stuck dashboard, so an operator who relies on `clawctl agent stop`
    74:     # could be left with the dashboard still bound to its loopback port.
    75:     # Only enforce when the dashboard unit is actually installed.
    76:     - name: Verify hermes dashboard process is stopped
    77:       ansible.builtin.command:
    78:         cmd: pgrep -u {{ agent_name }} -f "hermes dashboard"
    79:       register: dashboard_process_check
    80:       changed_when: false
    81:       failed_when: dashboard_process_check.rc == 0
    82:       when: dashboard_unit_file.stat.exists

    84:     - name: Display success message
    85:       ansible.builtin.debug:
    86:         msg: "Hermes service {{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }} stopped and disabled. ~/.hermes/ preserved."

     3: #   - MEMORY.md  (agent notes, ≤ 2200 chars)  → ~/.hermes/memories/

    15:       USER.md: 1375
    16:       SOUL.md: 3000
    17:     # SOUL.md lives at ~/.hermes/SOUL.md; others at ~/.hermes/memories/

    19:       {{ '/home/' + agent_name + '/.hermes'
    20:          if memory_filename == 'SOUL.md'
    21:          else '/home/' + agent_name + '/.hermes/memories' }}
    22:   tasks:
    23:     # Defense-in-depth: Python core/memory.py already validates agent_name,
    24:     # but a tampered Ansible inventory could still bypass that. Reject
    25:     # anything that does not match the same pattern enforced in Python
    26:     # (^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$) before we use it in a filesystem path.
    27:     - name: Validate agent_name format
    28:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    29:         msg: "Invalid agent_name format"
    30:       when:
    31:         - agent_name is not match('^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$')
    32: 
    33:     - name: Validate memory filename pattern
    34:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    35:         msg: "Invalid memory filename"
    36:       when:
    37:         - memory_filename is not match('^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)?$')
    38: 
    39:     - name: Reject path-traversal components
    40:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    41:         msg: "Invalid memory filename: traversal components not allowed"
    42:       when:
    43:         - memory_filename.split('/') | intersect(['', '.', '..']) | length > 0
    44: 
    45:     - name: Restrict to hermes memory allowlist
    46:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    47:         msg: "hermes memory accepts only MEMORY.md, USER.md, and SOUL.md"
    48:       when:
    49:         - memory_filename not in ['MEMORY.md', 'USER.md', 'SOUL.md']
    50: 
    51:     - name: Decode content for length validation
    52:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    53:         memory_decoded_content: "{{ memory_content_b64 | b64decode }}"
    54:       no_log: true
    55: 
    56:     - name: Enforce hermes per-file character limit
    57:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    58:         msg: >-
    59:           hermes memory file '{{ memory_filename }}' exceeds character limit
    60:           ({{ memory_decoded_content | length }} >
    61:           {{ memory_char_limits[memory_filename] }} chars)
    62:       when:
    63:         - memory_decoded_content | length > memory_char_limits[memory_filename]
    64: 
    65:     # Unset the decoded-content fact: Ansible facts can be persisted via the
    66:     # fact cache, and we have already used the value for length validation.
    67:     # The base64 form is re-decoded by the copy task below from the original
    68:     # extravar, so no information is lost.
    69:     - name: Drop decoded content from facts
    70:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    71:         memory_decoded_content: ""
    72:       no_log: true
    73: 
    74:     - name: Ensure target directory exists
    75:       ansible.builtin.file:
    76:         path: "{{ memory_target_dir | trim }}"
    77:         state: directory
    78:         owner: "{{ agent_name }}"
    79:         group: "{{ agent_name }}"
    80:         mode: "0700"
    81: 
    82:     # Drop any leftover staging file before write. A leftover symlink from
    83:     # a previous run (or planted by a local attacker between this play's
    84:     # tasks) would otherwise let `copy` follow the symlink to an
    85:     # attacker-chosen target. `state: absent` removes the path whether it
    86:     # is a symlink or a real file without following it.
    87:     - name: Clear any stale staging file
    88:       ansible.builtin.file:
    89:         path: "{{ memory_target_dir | trim }}/.{{ memory_filename }}.tmp"
    90:         state: absent
    91: 
    92:     - name: Write memory file content to staging path
    93:       # Stage to ".<file>.tmp" then atomically rename so a concurrent
    94:       # hermes daemon reader observes either the old or new content but
    95:       # never a partial write. Content is passed as base64 from Python
    96:       # so user-supplied bytes are never interpreted as Jinja2.
    97:       ansible.builtin.copy:
    98:         content: "{{ memory_content_b64 | b64decode }}"
    99:         dest: "{{ memory_target_dir | trim }}/.{{ memory_filename }}.tmp"
   100:         owner: "{{ agent_name }}"
   101:         group: "{{ agent_name }}"
   102:         mode: "0600"
   103:       no_log: true
   104: 
   105:     # TOCTOU guard: between `copy` and `mv`, a local attacker with write
   106:     # access to the target directory could swap the staging file for a
   107:     # symlink to an attacker-chosen path. Verify the staging file is a
   108:     # regular file (not a symlink) right before the rename.
   109:     - name: Verify staging file is a regular file (TOCTOU guard)
   110:       ansible.builtin.stat:
   111:         path: "{{ memory_target_dir | trim }}/.{{ memory_filename }}.tmp"
   112:         follow: false
   113:       register: hermes_staging_stat
   114: 
   115:     - name: Fail if staging file is a symlink or missing
   116:       ansible.builtin.fail:
   117:         msg: "Staging file is not a regular file (possible TOCTOU symlink race)"
   118:       when:
   119:         - not (hermes_staging_stat.stat.exists | default(false))
   120:           or (hermes_staging_stat.stat.islnk | default(false))
   121:           or not (hermes_staging_stat.stat.isreg | default(false))
   122: 
   123:     - name: Atomically replace memory file
   124:       # `mv` on the same filesystem is an atomic rename(2). The staging
   125:       # file shares the target directory so the rename never crosses
   126:       # filesystems.
   127:       ansible.builtin.command:
   128:         cmd: >-
   129:           mv -f
   130:           {{ memory_target_dir | trim }}/.{{ memory_filename }}.tmp
   131:           {{ memory_target_dir | trim }}/{{ memory_filename }}
   132:       changed_when: true
   133:       no_log: true

name: ansible/tasks/adsb-stack.yml
review_question: Would an Ansible expert judge this playbook or task file as needing abstraction because it contains too many direct leaf tasks?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Observability for the ADS-B receiver.
     3: #
     4: # dump1090-fa keeps the RTL-SDR and keeps feeding Flightradar24. Ultrafeeder
     5: # runs readsb in net-only mode off dump1090-fa's Beast output on port 30005
     6: # and adds the tar1090 map, graphs1090 and a Prometheus endpoint; DockTail
     7: # publishes the map on the tailnet over HTTPS. Prometheus and Grafana live on
     8: # hogsmeade (docker/prometheus-grafana, deployed by Arcane).
     9: - name: Ensure /docker exists
    10:   ansible.builtin.file:
    11:     path: /docker
    12:     state: directory
    13:     owner: root
    14:     group: root
    15:     mode: "0755"
    16: 
    17: - name: Ensure stack directories exist
    18:   ansible.builtin.file:
    19:     path: "/docker/{{ item }}"
    20:     state: directory
    21:     owner: root
    22:     group: root
    23:     mode: "0755"
    24:   loop:
    25:     - adsb
    26:     - docktail
    27: 
    28: - name: Copy compose files
    29:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    30:     src: "{{ playbook_dir }}/../docker/{{ item }}/compose.yaml"
    31:     dest: "/docker/{{ item }}/compose.yaml"
    32:     owner: root
    33:     group: root
    34:     mode: "0644"
    35:   loop:
    36:     - adsb
    37:     - docktail
    38: 
    39: # Written straight from the playbook's sops-decrypted environment: unlike
    40: # hogsmeade there is no Arcane pre-deploy hook here, so nothing needs the age
    41: # key on the host.
    42: - name: Write ADS-B stack environment
    43:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    44:     content: |
    45:       ADSB_LAT={{ adsb_lat }}
    46:       ADSB_LON={{ adsb_lon }}
    47:       ADSB_ALT_M={{ adsb_alt_m }}
    48:     dest: /docker/adsb/.env
    49:     owner: root
    50:     group: root
    51:     mode: "0600"
    52:   no_log: true
    53: 
    54: - name: Write DockTail environment
    55:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    56:     content: |
    57:       TAILSCALE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID={{ tailscale_oauth_client_id }}
    58:       TAILSCALE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET={{ tailscale_oauth_client_secret }}
    59:     dest: /docker/docktail/.env
    60:     owner: root
    61:     group: root
    62:     mode: "0600"
    63:   no_log: true
    64: 
    65: - name: Deploy ADS-B stack
    66:   community.docker.docker_compose_v2:
    67:     project_src: /docker/adsb
    68:     # The image tag is pinned, so there is nothing to re-pull on every run —
    69:     # and a ~600 MB pull is not free on a Pi's SD card.
    70:     pull: missing
    71:     state: present
    72: 
    73: - name: Deploy DockTail
    74:   community.docker.docker_compose_v2:
    75:     project_src: /docker/docktail
    76:     pull: missing
    77:     state: present

review_question: Would an Ansible expert judge this playbook or task file as needing abstraction because it contains too many direct leaf tasks?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Purpose: Block a joining node from reporting success until its Cilium agent is healthy
     3: # Dependencies: none (node-local — joining nodes have no kubeconfig)
     4: # Usage: Included by deploy_cluster/main.yaml for non-first nodes
     5: # Tags: [rke2, cilium, deploy_cluster]
     6: 
     7: # Without this, bloom reports success on a joining node the instant systemd
     8: # accepts the rke2 unit start. Everything after that point in the run is
     9: # FIRST_NODE-gated, so a node whose Cilium agent never came up exits bloom
    10: # cleanly and looks Ready, while the DaemonSet pods placed on it during that
    11: # window may be permanently wedged. Failing here converts a silent, days-long
    12: # latent fault into an immediate one.
    13: #
    14: # The agent is hostNetwork, so its own readiness endpoint is reachable from the
    15: # host netns without a kubeconfig — this is the same probe the cilium DaemonSet
    16: # uses for readinessProbe.
    17: #
    18: # use_proxy: no is required, not cosmetic: ansible's uri does not bypass
    19: # 127.0.0.1 on its own, so on a host with http_proxy set every attempt would be
    20: # sent to the proxy and fail.
    21: #
    22: # timeout is set explicitly because the default is 30s, and the port is filtered
    23: # rather than refused while the agent is starting — leaving it at the default
    24: # would stretch the retry budget below from ~20 minutes to over an hour.
    25: - name: Wait for the Cilium agent to report healthy on this node
    26:   uri:
    27:     url: http://127.0.0.1:9879/healthz
    28:     headers:
    29:       brief: "true"
    30:     status_code: 200
    31:     use_proxy: no
    32:     timeout: 5
    33:   register: cilium_healthz
    34:   until: cilium_healthz.status | default(0) == 200
    35:   retries: 90
    36:   delay: 10

name: roles/splunk_common/tasks/configure_input_cert.yml
review_question: Would an Ansible expert judge this playbook or task file as needing abstraction because it contains too many direct leaf tasks?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Configure Splunk input (S2S) certificate from operator-mounted TLS secret.
     3: # Input: /mnt/tls/splunk-input-tls-cert/{tls.crt, tls.key[, ca.crt]}
     4: # Output: bundled PEM at /opt/splunk/etc/auth/input-bundle.pem
     5: #         CA at /opt/splunk/etc/auth/splunk-input-ca.pem
     6: #         inputs.conf [SSL] configured
     7: 
     8: - name: Generate ephemeral SSL passphrase for input cert
     9:   command: >
    10:     python3 -c
    11:     "import secrets, base64; print(base64.b64encode(secrets.token_bytes(40)).decode())"
    12:   register: input_ssl_passphrase
    13:   changed_when: false
    14:   no_log: true
    15: 
    16: - name: Ensure Splunk auth directory exists
    17:   file:
    18:     path: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/auth"
    19:     state: directory
    20:     owner: "{{ splunk.user }}"
    21:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"
    22:     mode: '0700'
    23:   become: yes
    24:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
    25: 
    26: - name: Write input cert bundle script
    27:   copy:
    28:     dest: /tmp/splunk_bundle_input_cert.py
    29:     content: |
    30:       from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization import (
    31:           load_pem_private_key, Encoding, PrivateFormat, BestAvailableEncryption
    32:       )
    33:       import sys
    34: 
    35:       passphrase = sys.argv[1].encode()
    36:       key_path   = '/mnt/tls/splunk-input-tls-cert/tls.key'
    37:       cert_path  = '/mnt/tls/splunk-input-tls-cert/tls.crt'
    38:       out_path   = sys.argv[2] + '/etc/auth/input-bundle.pem'
    39: 
    40:       with open(key_path, 'rb') as f:
    41:           key = load_pem_private_key(f.read(), password=None)
    42: 
    43:       enc_key_pem = key.private_bytes(
    44:           Encoding.PEM,
    45:           PrivateFormat.PKCS8,
    46:           BestAvailableEncryption(passphrase)
    47:       )
    48: 
    49:       with open(cert_path, 'rb') as f:
    50:           cert_pem = f.read()
    51: 
    52:       with open(out_path, 'wb') as f:
    53:           f.write(cert_pem)
    54:           if not cert_pem.endswith(b'\n'):
    55:               f.write(b'\n')
    56:           f.write(enc_key_pem)
    57:     mode: '0700'
    58: 
    59: - name: Encrypt private key and build input cert bundle
    60:   command: >
    61:     python3 /tmp/splunk_bundle_input_cert.py
    62:     {{ input_ssl_passphrase.stdout }} {{ splunk.home }}
    63:   become: yes
    64:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
    65:   no_log: true
    66: 
    67: - name: Set input bundle permissions
    68:   file:
    69:     path: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/auth/input-bundle.pem"
    70:     owner: "{{ splunk.user }}"
    71:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"
    72:     mode: '0600'
    73:   become: yes
    74:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
    75: 
    76: - name: Check if ca.crt is present in input cert mount
    77:   stat:
    78:     path: /mnt/tls/splunk-input-tls-cert/ca.crt
    79:   register: input_ca_file
    80: 
    81: - name: Set sslRootCAPath to system bundle when ca.crt is absent
    82:   set_fact:
    83:     input_ca_path: /etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/pem/tls-ca-bundle.pem
    84:   when: not input_ca_file.stat.exists
    85: 
    86: - name: Write CA trust bundle script
    87:   copy:
    88:     dest: /tmp/splunk_build_input_ca_bundle.py
    89:     content: |
    90:       # tls.crt from the operator-mounted secret may contain intermediate
    91:       # certs that are not repeated in ca.crt (e.g. Vault PKI issuers put
    92:       # only the root in ca.crt). Splunk requires the full chain to be
    93:       # present locally in sslRootCAPath -- it does not complete the chain
    94:       # using intermediates presented by the peer during the handshake.
    95:       # Assemble tls.crt's non-leaf certs + ca.crt into one deduplicated
    96:       # trust bundle.
    97:       import sys
    98: 
    99:       tls_crt_path = '/mnt/tls/splunk-input-tls-cert/tls.crt'
   100:       ca_crt_path = '/mnt/tls/splunk-input-tls-cert/ca.crt'
   101:       out_path = sys.argv[1] + '/etc/auth/splunk-input-ca.pem'
   102: 
   103:       def split_pem_certs(data):
   104:           certs = []
   105:           current = []
   106:           for line in data.splitlines(keepends=True):
   107:               if line.strip() == b'-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----':
   108:                   current = [line]
   109:               elif line.strip() == b'-----END CERTIFICATE-----':
   110:                   current.append(line)
   111:                   certs.append(b''.join(current))
   112:                   current = []
   113:               elif current:
   114:                   current.append(line)
   115:           return certs
   116: 
   117:       with open(tls_crt_path, 'rb') as f:
   118:           tls_certs = split_pem_certs(f.read())
   119:       chain_certs = tls_certs[1:]  # drop the leaf; keep any presented intermediates/root
   120: 
   121:       with open(ca_crt_path, 'rb') as f:
   122:           ca_certs = split_pem_certs(f.read())
   123: 
   124:       seen = set()
   125:       ordered = []
   126:       for cert in chain_certs + ca_certs:
   127:           if cert not in seen:
   128:               seen.add(cert)
   129:               ordered.append(cert)
   130: 
   131:       with open(out_path, 'wb') as f:
   132:           for cert in ordered:
   133:               f.write(cert)
   134:               if not cert.endswith(b'\n'):
   135:                   f.write(b'\n')
   136:     mode: '0700'
   137:   when: input_ca_file.stat.exists
   138: 
   139: - name: Build input CA trust bundle
   140:   command: >
   141:     python3 /tmp/splunk_build_input_ca_bundle.py
   142:     {{ splunk.home }}
   143:   become: yes
   144:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   145:   changed_when: true
   146:   when: input_ca_file.stat.exists
   147: 
   148: - name: Set CA trust bundle permissions
   149:   file:
   150:     path: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/auth/splunk-input-ca.pem"
   151:     owner: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   152:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"
   153:     mode: '0644'
   154:   become: yes
   155:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   156:   when: input_ca_file.stat.exists
   157: 
   158: - name: Set sslRootCAPath to the assembled CA trust bundle
   159:   set_fact:
   160:     input_ca_path: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/auth/splunk-input-ca.pem"
   161:   when: input_ca_file.stat.exists
   162: 
   163: - name: Configure serverCert in inputs.conf [SSL]
   164:   ini_file:
   165:     dest: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/system/local/inputs.conf"
   166:     section: SSL
   167:     option: serverCert
   168:     value: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/auth/input-bundle.pem"
   169:     owner: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   170:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"
   171:   become: yes
   172:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   173: 
   174: - name: Configure sslPassword in inputs.conf [SSL]
   175:   ini_file:
   176:     dest: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/system/local/inputs.conf"
   177:     section: SSL
   178:     option: sslPassword
   179:     value: "{{ input_ssl_passphrase.stdout }}"
   180:     owner: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   181:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"
   182:   become: yes
   183:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   184:   no_log: true
   185:   changed_when: false
   186: 
   187: - name: Configure sslRootCAPath in inputs.conf [SSL]
   188:   ini_file:
   189:     dest: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/system/local/inputs.conf"
   190:     section: SSL
   191:     option: sslRootCAPath
   192:     value: "{{ input_ca_path }}"
   193:     owner: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   194:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"
   195:   become: yes
   196:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   197: 
   198: # enable_s2s.yml (legacy S2S flow) may have already written the deprecated
   199: # rootCA key to this same [SSL] stanza, pointing at $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/auth/cacert.pem
   200: # regardless of the operator-mounted cert. Overwrite it here so the two SSL
   201: # trust settings in inputs.conf agree.
   202: - name: Configure rootCA in inputs.conf [SSL] to match sslRootCAPath
   203:   ini_file:
   204:     dest: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/system/local/inputs.conf"
   205:     section: SSL
   206:     option: rootCA
   207:     value: "{{ input_ca_path }}"
   208:     owner: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   209:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"
   210:   become: yes
   211:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"

    50:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    51:     # yamllint disable-line rule:line-length
    52:     hpctests_hplsolo_N: "{{ ((((((hpctests_nodeinfo.info['MEMORY'][0] | int) * (hpctests_hpl_mem_frac | float) * 1024 * 1024 * 1) / 8) | root) / hpctests_hpl_NB)

    57:       | float) * 100 }}% of {{ hpctests_nodeinfo.info['MEMORY'][0] }} MB memory per node, block size (NB) = {{ hpctests_hpl_NB }}, problem size (N) = {{ hpctests_hplsolo_N

    59:     # yamllint enable rule:line-length
    60:

    75:     remote_src: true

    80:     dest: "{{ hpctests_rootdir }}/hpl-solo/HPL.dat"
    81:     mode: "0644"
    82:   vars:
    83:     hpctests_hpl_N: "{{ hpctests_hplsolo_N }}"
    84:     hpctests_hpl_P: "{{ hpctests_hplsolo_pq.grid.P }}"
    85:     hpctests_hpl_Q: "{{ hpctests_hplsolo_pq.grid.Q }}"
    86: 
    87: - name: Create sbatch script
    88:   ansible.builtin.template:
    89:     src: hpl-solo.sh.j2
    90:     dest: "{{ hpctests_rootdir }}/hpl-solo/hpl-solo.sh"
    91:     mode: "0755"
    92:   vars:
    93:     hpctests_hplsolo_ntasks: 2 # TODO: FIXME
    94: 
    95: - name: Remove previous outputs # noqa: no-changed-when
    96:   # As depending on the number of nodes there will be different numbers of output files for different partitions so won't all get overwritten
    97:   ansible.builtin.shell:
    98:     cmd: "rm -f {{ hpctests_rootdir }}/hpl-solo/hpl-solo.sh.*.out"
    99: 
   100: - name: Run hpl-solo # noqa: no-changed-when
   101:   ansible.builtin.command: bash -l -c 'sbatch --wait hpl-solo.sh'
   102:   args:
   103:     chdir: "{{ hpctests_rootdir }}/hpl-solo"
   104:   async: "{{ 20 * 60 }}" # wait for up to 20 minutes
   105:   poll: 15 # check every 15 seconds
   106:   register: hpctests_hplsolo_sbatch
   107: 
   108: - name: Check HPL completed OK
   109:   tags: postpro
   110:   ansible.builtin.shell: "grep '1 tests completed and passed residual checks' *.out"
   111:   args:
   112:     chdir: "{{ hpctests_rootdir }}/hpl-solo"

   114:   register: passed
   115:   failed_when: "passed.stdout_lines | length != hpctests_computes.stdout_lines | length"

   117: - name: Extract performance
   118:   # example of HPL output block - NB code review shows T/V can start with WR or WC:
   119:   #   <snip>
   120:   #   T/V                N    NB     P     Q               Time                 Gflops
   121:   #   --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   122:   #   WC00C2R2      110592   256     1     1            2545.90            3.54199e+02
   123:   #   HPL_pdgesv() start time Thu Feb 25 19:58:25 2021
   124:   #   <snip>
   125:   tags: postpro
   126:   ansible.builtin.shell: "set -o pipefail && grep '^W[R|C]' *.out | tr -s ' ' | cut -d ' ' -f 7"
   127:   args:
   128:     chdir: "{{ hpctests_rootdir }}/hpl-solo"
   129:   changed_when: false
   130:   register: perf
   131: 
   132: - name: Summarise results
   133:   tags: postpro
   134:   ansible.builtin.debug:
   135:     # yamllint disable rule:line-length
   136:     msg: |
   137:       Summary for hpl-solo on {{ hpctests_computes.stdout_lines | length }} nodes in '{{ hpctests_partition }}' partition, job ID {{ hpctests_hplsolo_sbatch.stdout.split()[-1] }}, device '{{ hpctests_ucx_net_devices }}':
   138: 
   139:         Max:  {{ perf.stdout_lines | map('float') | max }} gflops
   140:         Min:  {{ perf.stdout_lines | map('float') | min }} gflops

   144:       {{ dict(hpctests_computes.stdout_lines | zip(perf.stdout_lines | map('float'))) | to_nice_yaml }}
   145:     # yamllint enable rule:line-length

     8: #   * removes ONLY caches, logs and disposable build artifacts
     9: #   * NEVER touches Docker volumes or bind-mount data directories
    10: #     (postgres_data, keycloak-database, vault/raft, opensearch, ...)
    11: #   * skips any host that is currently executing a CI job
    12: #   * every riskier step sits behind its own toggle, disabled by default
    13: #
    14: # Usage:
    15: #   ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini plays/fleet-disk-cleanup.yaml
    16: #   ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini plays/fleet-disk-cleanup.yaml --check
    17: #   ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini plays/fleet-disk-cleanup.yaml --limit shuffle

    33:     cleanup_user: "{{ cleanup_runner_user | default('gh-runner') }}"

    36:     cleanup_force: false          # true = clean even while a CI job is running

    38:     # --- Reporting ---
    39:     monitored_mounts: ['/', '/home', '/var']
    40:     report_usage_threshold: 80    # du top-N diagnosis for mounts still above this
    41:     du_top_n: 10
    42: 
    43:     # --- Retention ---
    44:     journal_keep: "200M"          # shrink the systemd journal to this size now
    45:     journal_max_use: "200M"       # ... and cap it persistently in journald.conf
    46:     diag_log_age_days: 3          # delete actions-runner/_diag/*.log older than X
    47:     log_archive_age_days: 7       # delete rotated /var/log archives older than X
    48:     snap_refresh_retain: 2        # keep this many old snap revisions
    49: 
    50:     # --- Toggles (default = safe) ---
    51:     clean_journal: true
    52:     clean_journal_persistent: true  # write SystemMaxUse to journald.conf
    53:     clean_docker: true            # stopped containers, dangling images, build cache
    54:     clean_go_cache: true          # go clean -cache -modcache -testcache (as runner user)
    55:     clean_runner_diag: true       # old _diag logs
    56:     clean_runner_work_temp: true  # _work/_temp (job scratch, recreated on demand)
    57:     clean_trivy_cache: true

review_question: Would an Ansible expert judge this playbook or task file as needing abstraction because it contains too many direct leaf tasks?
source_context:
1: # Algorithm:
     2: # 1. `hostname` is already asserted defined/non-empty by destroy-vm.yml's
     3: #    shared pre_task.
     4: # 2. Check if the autogenerated inventory exists; load it if present, else
     5: #    init empty.
     6: # 3. Fail loudly if hostname is absent from inventory (unknown hostname),
     7: #    before any AWS action.
     8: # 4. Capture ansible_host (the instance's public IP) and aws_instance_id for
     9: #    hostname before the entry is removed.
    10: # 5. Load the AWS region default; check the instance's current state via
    11: #    amazon.aws.ec2_instance_info; terminate it if present and not already
    12: #    terminated, else warn that the inventory entry is stale and skip
    13: #    termination.
    14: # 6. Idempotent known_hosts cleanup for the captured IP (both paths).
    15: # 7. Remove the hostname from the autogenerated inventory and write it back.
    16: # The shared ansible-sg security group is left untouched (FR-013).
    17: ---
    18: - name: Check if AWS autogenerated inventory exists
    19:   ansible.builtin.stat:
    20:     path: "{{ playbook_dir }}/../inventories/aws_autogenerated.yml"
    21:   register: autogen_inv_stat
    22: 
    23: - name: Load AWS autogenerated inventory
    24:   ansible.builtin.include_vars:
    25:     file: "{{ playbook_dir }}/../inventories/aws_autogenerated.yml"
    26:     name: current_inventory
    27:   when: autogen_inv_stat.stat.exists
    28: 
    29: - name: Initialize empty inventory when autogenerated file is absent
    30:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    31:     current_inventory:
    32:       all:
    33:         hosts: {}
    34:       linux:
    35:         hosts: {}
    36:       aws:
    37:         hosts: {}
    38:   when: not autogen_inv_stat.stat.exists
    39: 
    40: - name: Fail if hostname is not present in AWS inventory
    41:   ansible.builtin.fail:
    42:     msg: >-
    43:       Hostname '{{ hostname }}' is not present in
    44:       inventories/aws_autogenerated.yml. Nothing to destroy.
    45:   when: hostname not in (current_inventory.all.hosts | default({}))
    46: 
    47: - name: Capture instance details for cleanup
    48:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    49:     aws_instance_ip: "{{ current_inventory.all.hosts[hostname].ansible_host }}"
    50:     aws_instance_id: "{{ current_inventory.all.hosts[hostname].aws_instance_id }}"
    51: 
    52: - name: Set aws known_hosts file path
    53:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    54:     aws_known_hosts_file: "{{ (playbook_dir + '/../inventories/aws_known_hosts') | realpath }}"
    55: 
    56: - name: Load AWS region default
    57:   ansible.builtin.include_vars:
    58:     file: "{{ playbook_dir }}/vars/aws_defaults.yml"
    59: 
    60: - name: Resolve AWS region
    61:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    62:     aws_resolved_region: "{{ aws_region | default(aws_default_region) }}"
    63: 
    64: - name: Check current state of EC2 instance
    65:   amazon.aws.ec2_instance_info:
    66:     instance_ids:
    67:       - "{{ aws_instance_id }}"
    68:     region: "{{ aws_resolved_region }}"
    69:   register: aws_instance_info
    70:   failed_when: false
    71: 
    72: - name: Determine whether EC2 instance is still present
    73:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    74:     aws_instance_still_present: >-
    75:       {{
    76:         (aws_instance_info.instances | default([]) | length > 0) and
    77:         (aws_instance_info.instances[0].state.name not in ['terminated', 'shutting-down'])
    78:       }}
    79: 
    80: - name: Warn if instance is absent from AWS (stale inventory entry)
    81:   ansible.builtin.debug:
    82:     msg: >-
    83:       WARNING: EC2 instance '{{ aws_instance_id }}' for hostname '{{ hostname }}'
    84:       does not exist or is already terminated in AWS but is present in
    85:       inventory. Proceeding with inventory cleanup only.
    86:   when: not aws_instance_still_present
    87: 
    88: - name: Terminate EC2 instance
    89:   amazon.aws.ec2_instance:
    90:     state: absent
    91:     instance_ids:
    92:       - "{{ aws_instance_id }}"
    93:     region: "{{ aws_resolved_region }}"
    94:     wait: true
    95:   when: aws_instance_still_present
    96: 
    97: - name: Check for known_hosts entry for destroyed instance IP
    98:   ansible.builtin.command:
    99:     cmd: "ssh-keygen -f {{ aws_known_hosts_file }} -F {{ aws_instance_ip }}"
   100:   register: aws_known_hosts_check
   101:   failed_when: false
   102:   changed_when: false
   103: 
   104: - name: Remove known_hosts entry for destroyed instance IP
   105:   ansible.builtin.command:
   106:     cmd: "ssh-keygen -f {{ aws_known_hosts_file }} -R {{ aws_instance_ip }}"
   107:   when: aws_known_hosts_check.stdout | trim | length > 0
   108:   failed_when: false
   109:   changed_when: true
   110: 
   111: - name: Build cleaned inventory without destroyed host
   112:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   113:     cleaned_inventory: >-
   114:       {{
   115:         {
   116:           'all': {
   117:             'hosts': (current_inventory.all.hosts | default({}) | dict2items
   118:                       | selectattr('key', '!=', hostname) | list | items2dict)
   119:           },
   120:           'linux': {
   121:             'hosts': (current_inventory.linux.hosts | default({}) | dict2items
   122:                       | selectattr('key', '!=', hostname) | list | items2dict)
   123:           },
   124:           'aws': {
   125:             'hosts': (current_inventory.aws.hosts | default({}) | dict2items
   126:                       | selectattr('key', '!=', hostname) | list | items2dict)
   127:           },
   128:           'basic': {
   129:             'hosts': ((current_inventory.basic | default({})).hosts | default({}) | dict2items
   130:                       | selectattr('key', '!=', hostname) | list | items2dict)
   131:           },
   132:           'desktop': {
   133:             'hosts': ((current_inventory.desktop | default({})).hosts | default({}) | dict2items
   134:                       | selectattr('key', '!=', hostname) | list | items2dict)
   135:           },
   136:           'windows': {
   137:             'hosts': ((current_inventory.windows | default({})).hosts | default({}) | dict2items
   138:                       | selectattr('key', '!=', hostname) | list | items2dict)
   139:           }
   140:         }
   141:       }}
   142: 
   143: - name: Write cleaned AWS inventory
   144:   ansible.builtin.copy:
   145:     content: "# AUTO-GENERATED — do not edit manually. Overwritten by create-vm.yml and destroy-vm.yml.\n{{ cleaned_inventory | to_nice_yaml(indent=2) }}"
   146:     dest: "{{ playbook_dir }}/../inventories/aws_autogenerated.yml"
   147:     mode: "0644"
   148: 
   149: - name: Assert hostname removed from AWS inventory
   150:   ansible.builtin.assert:
   151:     that: hostname not in (cleaned_inventory.all.hosts | default({}))
   152:     fail_msg: "Failed to remove '{{ hostname }}' from inventories/aws_autogenerated.yml"

    32:       name: clickhouse
    33:       group: clickhouse

    35:       create_home: false
    36:       state: present
    37: 
    38:   - name: Mkdir for data path

    40:       path: "{{ ch_data_path | default('/opt/clickhouse') }}"
    41:       state: directory
    42:       owner: clickhouse
    43:       group: clickhouse
    44: 
    45:   - name: Change data path
    46:     replace:
    47:       path: /etc/clickhouse-server/config.xml
    48:       regexp: 'path>(?:/var/lib/clickhouse|/opt/clickhouse|{{ ch_data_path | default("/opt/clickhouse") | regex_escape }})/'
    49:       replace: 'path>{{ ch_data_path | default("/opt/clickhouse") }}/'
    50:       backup: yes

    52:   - name: Change default port

    54:       path: /etc/clickhouse-server/config.xml
    55:       regexp: '^    <tcp_port>[^<>]*</tcp_port>'
    56:       replace: '    <tcp_port>{{ ch_port }}</tcp_port>'
    57:       backup: yes
    58: 
    59:   - name: Change clickhouse password
    60:     replace:
    61:       path: /etc/clickhouse-server/users.xml
    62:       regexp: '^\s+<password>[^<>]*</password>'
    63:       replace: '        <password>{{ ch_password }}</password>'
    64:       backup: yes
    65: 
    66:   - name: Allow remote hosts connect to clickhouse (config.xml)
    67:     lineinfile:
    68:       path: /etc/clickhouse-server/config.xml
    69:       insertafter: '<!-- <listen_host>::</listen_host> -->'
    70:       line: '    <listen_host>::</listen_host>'
    71:       state: present
    72:       backup: yes
    73: 
    74:   - name: Enlarge max mem usage (config.xml)
    75:     replace:
    76:       path: /etc/clickhouse-server/config.xml
    77:       regexp: '^\s+<max_server_memory_usage_to_ram_ratio>0\.\d+</max_server_memory_usage_to_ram_ratio>'
    78:       replace: '    <max_server_memory_usage_to_ram_ratio>2</max_server_memory_usage_to_ram_ratio>'

    81:   - name: Allow remote hosts connect to clickhouse (users.xml)

    86:       backup: yes
    87: 
    88:   - name: Allow User can create other users and grant rights to them (users.xml)

    90:       path: /etc/clickhouse-server/users.xml
    91:       regexp: '<!-- <access_management>1</access_management> -->'
    92:       replace: '<access_management>1</access_management>'
    93:       backup: yes
    94: 
    95:   - name: Allow drop large tables (config.xml)

    97:       path: /etc/clickhouse-server/config.xml
    98:       regexp: '<!-- <max_table_size_to_drop>0</max_table_size_to_drop> -->'

   106:
